keyFeatures: Embedded keyless free-models router
Automated self-correction loops with local test verification
Persistent local memory graph for project context
Fusion best-of-N and multi-agent orchestration modes
Provider-neutral support for local models and API keys
bestFor: Developers who prefer terminal-first workflows and require a privacy-focused, vendor-neutral agent that performs automated verification of code changes.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a full GUI-based IDE experience with features like real-time inline tab completion.
recentUpdates: Recent releases include version 0.3.15. Previous updates added Fusion mode for best-of-N orchestration, improved independent review commands, and refined background refreshing for the free-model catalog.
verdict: A powerful, privacy-focused coding agent that excels at verified task execution and avoiding vendor lock-in through its provider-neutral, terminal-first design.

name: Xirp
pricingDetail: Xirp desktop app (Free), Portal Foundations (Free for 60 days, then contact sales)
description: Xirp is a vendor-neutral agentic development environment that acts as a management layer for AI coding agents. It allows developers to run and orchestrate multiple agent sessions in parallel locally on macOS while maintaining persistent context across different models.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent session management in a unified interface
Vendor-neutral support for Claude, Gemini, Codex, Pi, and Cursor
Local Git worktree isolation for parallel task execution
Portal Workspace integration for shared organizational context
Cost alerting and usage tracking for agent sessions
bestFor: macOS developers who juggle multiple AI coding agents simultaneously and need to maintain state and organizational context across projects.
notIdealFor: Developers on Windows or Linux, users who only run a single agent for simple tasks, or teams requiring open-source software and production SLAs.
recentUpdates: Version 0.67.0 (2026-11-13) improved minimap card layouts and session status visibility; Version 0.66.0 (2026-11-12) introduced a tabbed session panel, Git view per session, and improved session composer workflows.
verdict: Xirp is a highly capable, vendor-agnostic tool for power users of AI coding agents that effectively solves the problem of context loss during complex, multi-agent workflows, though it is currently limited to macOS.

name: Kolkrabbi (kolk)
pricingDetail: The tool is open-source and free to use. It does not charge for its own service, though it integrates with your existing paid subscriptions (Claude Pro, ChatGPT Plus, GitHub Copilot) and third-party API providers like OpenRouter.
description: Kolkrabbi is an open-source, model-agnostic AI coding agent for the terminal that integrates multiple AI subscriptions and local models into a single session. It features three operational modes—chat, code, and agent—alongside an effort-based dial to manage model tiers and task complexity.
keyFeatures: Multi-subscription support for Claude, ChatGPT, and GitHub Copilot
Local model support via Ollama, vLLM, or OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Agent mode for task decomposition and concurrent orchestration
Local-only cost, latency, and performance tracking
Optional OS-level execution sandboxing via Seatbelt or Landlock
bestFor: Developers who need a terminal-based AI coding agent with the flexibility to switch between multiple LLM providers and local models while maintaining strict data privacy.
notIdealFor: Windows users, as it is primarily designed for macOS and Linux, or users requiring cloud-synced, GUI-based, or plug-and-play experiences.
recentUpdates: The tool transitioned from specific free-model presets to live free-model discovery via OpenRouter in October 2026, and version 1.3.7 was released on 2026-10-07.
verdict: A powerful, privacy-focused alternative to Claude Code that excels in flexibility and cost transparency, making it ideal for power users who want to manage their own AI toolchain.

name: FrontierAgent
pricingDetail: Free (Open-source under Apache-2.0). Users are responsible for model token costs via their own OpenAI-compatible API endpoint.
description: FrontierAgent is an open-source agent runtime and terminal TUI built for long-horizon research and file-based tasks. It features two primary workflows, ReAct and Agent Team, which operate within a task-scoped, fail-closed filesystem sandbox.
keyFeatures: Native ReAct and Agent Team workflow modes
Task-scoped filesystem sandbox for security
Live TUI task board with real-time progress tracking
Asynchronous human intervention and steering
Full execution tracing with local checkpointing and undo capabilities
bestFor: Developers and researchers performing multi-step research, file-heavy analysis, or those evaluating models in a local environment.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring stable tagged releases, deep LSP support, git-aware code editing, or environments that demand hardened security boundaries rather than file-level sandboxing.
recentUpdates: Recent repository activity includes fixes for shell descendant reaping, improved handling of quoted response filenames, and adjustments to how Agent Team gates track command approvals.
verdict: A transparent and highly capable research-oriented agent harness, though it is currently better suited for local experimentation and evaluation rather than critical production workflows due to the project's youth and lack of formal releases.

name: YYLO
pricingDetail: Free (open-source MIT license). Users pay separately for their chosen AI model provider usage.
description: YYLO is a local-first command-line orchestrator designed to manage AI coding agents, repeatable workflows, and repository changes. It provides structured task isolation, validation evidence, and guarded Git-native merge operations to coordinate development tasks without bundling the agents themselves.
keyFeatures: Orchestration of multiple AI coding agents
Typed task and merge lifecycle with Git worktrees
Content-addressed validation evidence for task inputs
Support for both inline loops and reusable YAML workflows
Durable receipt-backed records and terminal state manifests
bestFor: Development teams requiring controlled Git topology, auditable recovery, and structured workflows for AI-assisted coding.
notIdealFor: Solo developers looking for simple one-shot prompts without queueing or controller concepts, or teams seeking a GUI-first experience.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.15 (2026-11-24) updated Pi model shortcuts to use the latest models in the GPT family, including gpt-6.2-astra as the default, and aligned CLI documentation with provider routing tests.
verdict: YYLO is a powerful, free open-source orchestrator for developers who want to manage complex, multi-step AI coding workflows with high accountability, though it requires users to configure their own agents and handle model-related costs independently.

name: pi-agent-ide
pricingDetail: Free (MIT-licensed); users are responsible for their own model API usage costs.
description: Pi Agent IDE is an agent-native extension for the Pi coding agent that provides a unified set of tools for code understanding, editing, debugging, and system observation. It supports semantic operations on both local and remote SSH-based codebases with guarded editing and built-in rollback capabilities.
keyFeatures: Unified interface for reading, searching, and semantic editing
Persistent terminal sessions and interactive debugger support
Guarded snapshot-based editing with automatic rollback
LSP-based code analysis and navigation
Cross-platform support for local and remote SSH environments
bestFor: Developers using the Pi coding agent who need precise, tool-integrated control over code manipulation and debugging within complex projects.
notIdealFor: Users who require a highly stable, production-ready environment or built-in guardrails, as the tool is experimental and subject to frequent interface changes.
recentUpdates: Version 0.9.8 was published on 2026-11-08. Previous updates in October 2026 introduced focused search tools like ast_search and lsp_search, on-demand tool guidance, and refinements to VS Code debugger integration.
verdict: A powerful and highly capable experimental toolkit that provides superior semantic control for Pi-based AI coding workflows, recommended primarily for early adopters.

name: MiMo Code
pricingDetail: Open-source under MIT License with optional paid Token Plan subscriptions starting at $6/month and pay-as-you-go API access.
description: MiMo Code is a terminal-native AI coding agent developed by Xiaomi that understands codebases to plan changes, perform edits, and manage development workflows. It features a persistent memory system and supports multiple LLM providers, offering both build and planning modes for software development tasks.
keyFeatures: Persistent cross-session memory using SQLite FTS5
Subagent system with goal-based task tracking
Configurable context management with automatic checkpointing
Support for multiple LLM providers via API or Token Plan
Integrated workflows for research, fact-checking, and experimentation
bestFor: Solo developers and terminal-first engineers who require long-running sessions with persistent context and prefer open-weight models.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring SSO, role-based access control, audit logging, managed support SLAs, or those dependent on first-party IDE extensions.
recentUpdates: Version 0.1.13 (2026-08-19) focused on operational stability, introducing scoped OpenAI-compatible interfaces for TUI sessions and enhanced credential isolation for child processes.
verdict: A powerful, highly autonomous AI coding agent that excels at maintaining context over extended development cycles, making it a strong choice for professional productivity workflows.

name: molt
pricingDetail: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). You bring your own model: an API key for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Anthropic's API, a local model, or an existing Grok plan.
description: molt (desktop app branded Maat Agent) is an open-source coding agent with a terminal CLI/TUI and an Electron desktop app. When the model says a task is done, molt runs the project's done.yml checks against the real files on disk and refuses the claim if any check fails, sending the failure back to the model.
keyFeatures: Completion checks (tests, type checks, builds) defined in done.yml and run against the real disk
A receipt for every attempt, including refused ones
Before and after hashes on every file write, in a hash-chained journal that `molt verify` recomputes
Works with OpenAI-compatible endpoints (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) and Anthropic's API
Terminal UI, headless mode for CI, and a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
bestFor: Developers who want a coding agent whose "done" is checked against their own tests and builds rather than taken on the model's word.
notIdealFor: Users who want a hosted service with no API key or local model to set up, or projects without automated checks to verify against.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.2 ships the desktop app and CLI from one engine; builds are on the GitHub releases page.
verdict: A young open-source project focused on one thing: not accepting a coding agent's completion claim until project checks pass on disk.

name: Prime Agent
pricingDetail: Prime Agent is fully open-source and free to install, though users are responsible for the costs associated with the LLM providers they choose to use within the agent.
description: Prime Agent is an open-source coding and research agent designed for long-running autonomous tasks. It utilizes a Recursive Language Model that treats context as a variable within a persistent Python REPL and features a Continual Harness that allows the agent to refine its own skills and memories through iterative, evidence-backed updates.
keyFeatures: Recursive Language Model architecture with a persistent Python REPL
Continual Harness for self-improving prompts, skills, and memory
Daemon-backed sessions that survive terminal disconnection
Direct agent-to-agent communication and orchestration
Autonomous mode with configurable turn, token, and time budgets
bestFor: Long-running research and coding tasks where programmatic access to session history and autonomous self-refinement are prioritized.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring a secure, sandboxed environment for untrusted repositories or those seeking a simple, turn-based agent experience without a learning curve.
recentUpdates: Version 0.10.5, released on 2026-11-18, refined harness storage paths, improved skill discovery and loading, and updated Python kernel integration for local skills.
verdict: A powerful, highly technical, and extensible framework for complex autonomous agent workflows that excels in long-term tasks, though it requires careful management of user permissions due to its lack of a built-in sandbox.

name: CodeAF
pricingDetail: CodeAF is free (open-source under Apache 2.0). Users pay their own model providers for tokens, or use local models at no cost.
description: CodeAF is an open-source, terminal-based software factory designed to manage multiple coding agents and tasks simultaneously from a single window. It uses built-in specialists to handle coding changes, security audits, and pull request reviews while allowing users to automate workflows through standing orders and team-based management.
keyFeatures: Built-in specialists for coding (/senior-dev), security (/sec), and pull request review (/review)
Pareto crewing that automatically assigns models to specific tasks based on complexity and cost
Headless mode for integration into CI/CD pipelines and automated scripting
Persistent task management that continues running after the terminal is closed
Multi-project dashboard to monitor conversations and status across multiple repositories
bestFor: Developers looking to manage complex, multi-agent coding workflows or automated software engineering tasks that require project-wide coordination and persistence.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer a single-agent interactive chat experience that does not require managing teams of agents or setting up specific budgets and specialists.
recentUpdates: Version 0.8.3 released on 2026-11-19 introduced improved patience and handling for slow local models, ensuring they are not prematurely cut off or sent duplicate requests.
verdict: CodeAF is a highly capable, open-source terminal automation suite that excels at complex, project-wide engineering tasks, though it requires a steeper learning curve than simple conversational coding agents.

name: Herdr
pricingDetail: The app, herdr-core, and Herdr TUI are free and open source under the Apache 2.0 license. A service called Herdr Cloud is currently in development with a waitlist and no announced pricing.
description: Herdr is a terminal-based multiplexer designed to track and coordinate multiple coding agents running across local and remote machines. It allows developers to monitor agent status (idle, working, or blocked) in a centralized sidebar and maintains persistent sessions in the background even when the client is disconnected.
keyFeatures: Unified dashboard for monitoring multiple coding agents across local and remote SSH-connected machines
Persistent background runtime (herdr-core) that keeps agent sessions alive after closing the app or disconnecting
Agent status tracking (idle, working, blocked) via screen manifest detection or direct integration
Extensible plugin marketplace for custom themes, layouts, and workspace workflows
Cross-platform support for macOS, Windows, Linux, and mobile devices (iOS/Android) to check agent status
bestFor: Terminal-first developers who manage multiple concurrent AI agent sessions and need a persistent, unified way to monitor their progress and status across different machines.
notIdealFor: Users requiring enterprise-grade security compliance, centrally managed identity, contractual support, or those whose workflows rely primarily on browser-based UIs rather than terminal-native interfaces.
recentUpdates: In September 2026, Herdr raised a $6M seed round. Version 0.9 was released in September 2026, introducing the integration of local and remote machines into a single TUI client. Earlier in 2026, the project saw updates to session persistence, improved workspace navigation, and optimizations to reduce CPU usage.
verdict: Herdr is a highly effective, specialized runtime for power users who manage numerous AI coding agents and need a reliable, machine-agnostic infrastructure to keep their workflows organized and active.

name: Agent Deck
pricingDetail: Agent Deck is MIT-licensed and open-source. It does not sell AI usage or access to providers; users connect their own existing AI accounts and pay providers directly.
description: Agent Deck is a terminal-based session manager designed to oversee multiple AI coding agent sessions in a single interface. It provides status tracking, git worktree management, and unified MCP (Model Context Protocol) coordination for various CLI agents.
keyFeatures: Unified dashboard for monitoring status of multiple AI coding agents
Git worktree support for isolating parallel tasks
Real-time cost tracking dashboard across models and sessions
MCP manager for attaching servers globally or per-session
Conductor feature for Slack, Telegram, and Discord integration
bestFor: Developers managing multiple terminal-based AI coding sessions across different projects who need centralized status visibility and tool coordination.
notIdealFor: Beginners seeking a simple, all-in-one managed editor assistant or users who require a native Windows GUI application rather than a CLI/TUI environment.
recentUpdates: Version 1.16.40 (2026-11-22) introduced the Antigravity CLI as a built-in tool, an owner to-do list, and improvements to the recall timeline. Version 1.16.39 (2026-11-15) added standing orders for conductors, assistant bot connectivity, and improved session permission handling.
verdict: A powerful, highly modular hub for power users who rely on multiple AI coding CLI tools and need centralized observability, cost control, and persistent management.

name: Memdoor
pricingDetail: The Memdoor agent, decision model and workflows are free and open-source under Apache-2.0, with no account required. Pro ($10/month) adds end-to-end-encrypted remote control from your phone plus workflow state kept on memdoor.ai so workflows can depend on each other across machines. Every model call runs on your own provider key, ChatGPT plan or a local model.
description: Memdoor is a terminal coding agent and deterministic workflow runner shipped as one static Go binary. The agent reads files, edits code and runs checks, while YAML workflows coordinate parallel, check-gated steps with approval gates so repeatable work can run by hand, from CI or on a local schedule with cloud or local models.
keyFeatures: Deterministic YAML workflows with parallel steps and approval gates
Bring-your-own-key or local model support via Ollama, llama.cpp, and others
Headless CLI for integration with CI, cron, and shell scripts
Token-optimizing decision model that filters file reads and tool usage
End-to-end-encrypted remote terminal control
bestFor: Developers seeking a scriptable, model-agnostic coding agent that handles complex, repeatable, and verified tasks locally, over SSH, or in CI environments.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer a full-featured graphical IDE or a managed SaaS platform that includes built-in infrastructure and enterprise support.
recentUpdates: On November 2, 2026, releases v1.784.0 through v1.786.0 were deployed. On October 31, 2026, the tool's team-solve workflow achieved a mean score of 9.8/10 on selected LiveCodeBench Hard problems using Qwen3.8-27B agents.
verdict: A fast-moving, open-source agent that stands out for treating workflows as deterministic, check-verified pipelines and for making small local models competitive on coding tasks.

name: agent-mcts
pricingDetail: Free and open source under the MIT license. You pay only for the coding agent and model usage it drives; the run shows a node and dollar budget (for example 12 nodes / $10.00) before spending anything.
description: agent-mcts is a test-time search harness that wraps coding agent CLIs in a Monte Carlo Tree Search engine. It allows agents to explore multiple solution branches, backtrack from dead ends, and concentrate budget on the most promising paths to improve code fix reliability.
keyFeatures: Real Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with UCT selection and backtracking
Isolated execution environments using Git worktrees
Multi-strategy evaluation via test commands, LLM judges, or generated tests
Live terminal tree visualization with support for pausing, resuming, and parallel execution
Agent-agnostic architecture supporting Claude Code and Codex CLI
bestFor: Developers seeking more reliable code fixes for well-specified tasks where success can be verified by tests or automated judging.
notIdealFor: Quick one-off edits, tasks where token costs are a primary constraint, or vague bug reports without test coverage.
recentUpdates: Version 0.4.1 was released on 2026-11-22, following v0.4.0 (generated tests), and v0.3.0 which introduced LLM judging, parallel episode runs, and in-place run continuation via the resume command.
verdict: An early but working way to bring tree search to the coding agent you already use, with published benchmark caveats.

name: Trix
pricingDetail: Free and open source under the MIT licence. You pay only for the coding agents and model plans you run inside it.
description: Trix is a terminal-based workspace designed for running multiple coding agents simultaneously, providing visibility into their activity and status. It uses per-process hooks or screen heuristics to track whether an agent is working, needs human input, or has completed its task.
keyFeatures: Per-process agent state monitoring with status alerts and desktop notifications
Built-in Git worktree management for parallel agent task execution
Cost and token usage tracking for Claude and Codex agents
Integrated diff review, commit, and pull request workflows
Background server persistence for detached sessions and agent resumes
bestFor: Developers who manage multiple CLI-based AI coding agents in the terminal and need to monitor their progress and requirements efficiently.
notIdealFor: Users who require a graphical desktop application or those working in Windows environments, as Trix currently only supports Linux and macOS.
recentUpdates: Recent releases include version 1.5.0, which added agent cloning, enhanced layout persistence, and global instruction configurations, following the 1.4.3 release.
verdict: An agent-first terminal multiplexer with unusually deep per-agent state, review and cost tracking, moving fast in early releases.

name: Warp
pricingDetail: Free plan includes core terminal features with pay-as-you-go AI; Build plan is $20/month with 1,500 AI credits and extra collaboration features; Business and Enterprise plans offer per-seat pricing, SSO, and custom controls.
description: Warp is an agentic development environment featuring a modern terminal, a built-in coding agent, and cloud automation. It integrates local command-line work with cloud-based software factories and supports third-party CLI agents within its interface.
keyFeatures: Modern terminal with block-based output and IDE-like editing
Built-in Warp Agent for multi-step tasks and shell command execution
Warp Agent CLI for use in any terminal or over SSH
Support for third-party CLI agents like Claude Code and Codex
Warp Factories for building automated, repeatable software workflows
bestFor: Terminal-heavy developers who want a unified environment to run, monitor, and collaborate on both built-in and third-party coding agents.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a fully offline terminal, organizations with strict data-residency requirements, or developers looking for a lightweight terminal without cloud or account dependencies.
recentUpdates: On October 15, 2026, Warp added support for Muse Code as a CLI agent and enabled cloud agents to save handoff snapshots. On August 27, 2026, the Warp Factories infrastructure entered Early Access.
verdict: Warp is a powerful, highly integrated tool that successfully transforms the standard terminal into an advanced, agent-native development workspace, though users should be mindful of its usage-based credit model for AI features.

name: Wave
pricingDetail: The core terminal is open-source, free to use, and requires no login or subscription. Future monetization is planned via opt-in team collaboration features, while the current AI implementation provides included credits with a Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) option for heavy users.
description: Wave is an open-source, AI-native terminal that integrates terminal blocks with file previews, web browsing, and a built-in GUI editor. It is designed to function as a unified, widget-based workspace that runs entirely on the user's machine.
keyFeatures: Durable SSH sessions that survive network interruptions and restarts
Multi-modal AI assistant with local model, BYOK, and vision support
Integrated GUI editor for remote and local file editing
Widget-based workspace with support for file previews, dashboards, and web browsing
Advanced SSH management with support for ProxyJump, WSL, and identity files
bestFor: Developers who want a highly visual, widget-based workspace that combines terminal sessions with integrated AI, file management, and web tools in a single interface.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer minimalist or high-performance native terminal emulators, or those requiring specific support for serial, Telnet, X11 forwarding, or advanced tunnel management.
recentUpdates: Recent releases (v0.14.x) introduced a new Process Viewer widget, Quake mode, vertical tab layouts, xterm.js v6 integration, and significant improvements to SSH session durability, AI provider flexibility, and RPC streaming performance.
verdict: Wave is an ambitious, modern terminal that excels at turning the command line into a visual, project-centric dashboard. While the block-based paradigm requires a shift in muscle memory, it offers a powerful environment for users who want to consolidate their entire toolchain into one cohesive, persistent workspace.

name: TermRover
pricingDetail: The core app is free, including SSH, Mosh, tmux, Herdr, Zellij, SFTP, and unlimited hosts. Pro is an optional upgrade for unlimited voice/image attachments, unlimited port forwards, and additional themes, available via a $24.99/year subscription or a $79.99 one-time lifetime purchase.
description: TermRover is an AI-native, mobile-first SSH and Mosh terminal designed to optimize the experience of working with tmux, Herdr, Rex, and Zellij on iOS and Android. It focuses on providing a natural, touch-optimized environment for interacting with remote coding agents, allowing users to send images, dictate prompts, and conduct voice calls with agents directly from the terminal.
keyFeatures: Native support for tmux, Herdr, Rex, and Zellij multiplexers with touch-optimized controls
SSH and Mosh connectivity with live transport switching
Voice-to-agent calling for Codex, Claude Code, pi, OMP, and OpenCode
Smart composer for multi-line prompts, image annotation, and dictation
Integrated SFTP file browser and port forwarding capabilities
bestFor: Developers who frequently manage remote sessions and coding agents from mobile devices and require reliable connectivity, touchscreen-specific TUI controls, and deep integration with terminal multiplexers.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a full-featured desktop-style environment, a platform with integrated agent-supervision dashboards/notifications, or those working on Windows machines where agent calling is unsupported.
recentUpdates: Version 1.5.2 introduced custom path support and improved Herdr layout management. Version 1.5.1 added support for the Rex multiplexer and enhanced port-forwarding. Version 1.5.0 initially brought Rex sessions, tabs, and native pane resizing to iOS and Android.
verdict: TermRover is a highly capable, terminal-first tool that excels at making mobile interaction with remote agents and multiplexers feel natural and efficient, offering a robust free tier that covers the most essential professional needs.

name: uniTerm
pricingDetail: Distributed under the Apache-2.0 license, making it free to use and modify.
description: uniTerm is a lightweight, all-in-one terminal emulator that supports over 30 connection protocols, including remote terminals, file transfers, remote desktops, database clients, and container management. It features a built-in autonomous AI agent capable of planning and executing multi-round shell commands directly within the terminal.
keyFeatures: Autonomous AI agent for multi-turn shell command planning and execution
Support for 30+ protocols including SSH, RDP, VNC, S3, Kubernetes, and various databases
Deep terminal integration with flexible execution modes and MCP server support
Cross-device cloud synchronization via Git or WebDAV
Network toolbox including traffic capture, firewall management, and port forwarding
bestFor: Developers and system administrators who require a unified, feature-dense workspace for managing diverse infrastructure and complex automated shell tasks.
notIdealFor: Users who require built-in team-sharing features or those who are unable or unwilling to configure external AI API keys for the agent functionalities.
recentUpdates: Version 1.12.4 (released 2026-11-21) added network traffic capture, remote firewall management, a dockable notes panel, and support for Devolutions RDM import.
verdict: A powerful, feature-dense terminal emulator that effectively bridges traditional remote management with modern AI-driven automation, suitable for professional power users.

name: cmux
pricingDetail: The native macOS terminal app is free and open-source. Paid plans include Pro ($50/mo or $40/mo billed yearly), Max ($200/mo or $160/mo billed yearly), and Team ($60/user/mo), which provide access to Cloud VMs and the iOS companion app.
description: cmux is a native macOS terminal built on the Ghostty rendering engine, specifically designed to help developers manage multiple AI coding agents. It provides a multitasking-focused interface featuring vertical tabs, split panes, an integrated browser, and a notification system that tracks agent status and activity.
keyFeatures: Vertical tabs and split panes with sidebar status monitoring
Agent notification system tracking terminal hooks
In-app programmable browser with scriptable API
Cloud VMs for remote agent execution
CLI and socket API for workspace automation
bestFor: macOS developers who run multiple concurrent AI coding agents and require centralized visibility into agent states and session management.
notIdealFor: Users on Windows or Linux operating systems, as cmux is currently a macOS-exclusive native application.
recentUpdates: Version 0.65.2 (October 14, 2026) added improvements for agent session restores, cloud stability, and sign-in reliability. Version 0.65.0 (October 5, 2026) introduced agent support on SSH hosts, crash-proof session restoration, predictive local echo for remote links, and an import tool for migrating terminal settings.
verdict: cmux is a highly effective, performance-oriented terminal for Mac users who struggle with context switching between multiple AI coding agents; its native UI and notification system significantly reduce the overhead of managing agent-driven development workflows.

name: Corgi
pricingDetail: Corgi is free and open-source under the MIT license; users consume their own existing provider accounts for AI model usage.
description: Corgi is an AI-native terminal multiplexer designed to manage multiple coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode in persistent, side-by-side terminal panes. It features an integrated status tracking system that alerts developers when agents require attention, alongside built-in support for Git worktrees and resource usage monitoring.
keyFeatures: Per-agent status badges and F1 quick-jump to active tasks
Persistent background sessions for agents and processes
Unified launcher for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode
Scriptable CLI for programmatic terminal control
Git worktree integration and per-workspace resource monitoring
bestFor: Developers who manage multiple AI coding agents simultaneously and need a centralized view for monitoring agent activity, token usage, and terminal persistence.
notIdealFor: Users who do not utilize AI coding agents, those requiring a stable, mature daily-driver terminal, or those needing native Windows support beyond WSL.
recentUpdates: The project launched and was open-sourced on October 23, 2026, followed by ongoing updates to the CLI, viewer, and terminal themes throughout October and November 2026.
verdict: Corgi is a promising, ergonomically focused tool for heavy terminal-agent users, though its status as a very young project means users should expect rough edges and consider it for non-critical workflows.

name: nodeterm
pricingDetail: The desktop app is free to download and use, including 5 relay bridges per month for off-network phone or peer connections. nodeterm Pro (subscription, also purchasable in the iOS app) removes the relay cap and unlocks Team Access for sharing a canvas with teammates by the seat. Source is published under the Business Source License 1.1 (each version converts to MIT after four years); agent CLIs and model plans are paid separately.
description: nodeterm is an AI-native terminal manager that organizes coding agents and terminals as interactive nodes on an infinite canvas. It leverages persistent tmux sessions to ensure work survives app restarts and machine reboots, allowing developers to manage parallel agent workflows spatially.
keyFeatures: Spatial canvas and kanban board views for managing agent sessions
Persistent terminal sessions backed by tmux
Support for multiple AI coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini
E2E-encrypted relay for remote access via an iOS companion app
On-device voice transcription using Whisper for terminal interaction
bestFor: Developers running multiple parallel coding agents who prefer a spatial, visual workspace over traditional stacked terminal tabs.
notIdealFor: Users requiring an OSI-approved open-source license, or Windows users who need a production-ready experience, as the Windows build is currently in an unsigned beta state without full session continuity.
recentUpdates: Version 0.5.3 (2026-11-23) introduced quote-to-chat functionality, improved Claude subagent transcript reading, and added multi-select capabilities to the kanban board.
verdict: A fast-moving, feature-rich agent workspace whose canvas and kanban views make parallel agent sessions easier to track, provided its source-available license fits your use.

name: Harp
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (AGPL-3.0). Harp adds no servers of its own; upstream Warp AI and cloud features follow Warp's own terms.
description: Harp is an unofficial, open-source macOS fork of the Warp terminal that replaces the traditional tab bar with a sidebar optimized for managing multiple AI coding agents. It provides real-time status tracking for Claude Code and Codex sessions, alongside features like persistent tab groups and agent usage-limit monitoring.
keyFeatures: Sidebar-based agent status monitoring (working, waiting, done)
Usage-limit rings for Claude Code and Codex
Persistent tab groups with optional tmux integration
Bundled Claude Code status plugin for zero-setup monitoring
Automatic background updates from GitHub releases
bestFor: macOS developers who use Warp and need to manage multiple Claude Code or Codex sessions simultaneously.
notIdealFor: Users on Linux or Windows, those seeking official support from Warp, or users requiring agents other than Claude Code and Codex.
recentUpdates: Version 0.1.8 (October 29, 2026) introduced 'needs you' status indicators for Codex sessions and improved task name display in the sidebar. Version 0.1.7 (October 29, 2026) added native agent status tracking for Claude Code without requiring external configuration.
verdict: A focused, polished take on agent-aware tabs for Warp fans on macOS; young and single-maintainer, so treat it as an early unofficial fork.

name: Horus
pricingDetail: Free and open source under the MIT licence, distributed on F-Droid and GitHub Releases. You pay only for the Claude, OpenAI or OpenCode model plans you sign in to inside each agent.
description: Horus is an Android application that provides a full ARM64 Linux workspace (Alpine or Debian) with a native terminal to run coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode directly on your phone. It operates without requiring root access and supports background processing, allowing agents to continue tasks while the device is locked.
keyFeatures: Native Linux environment (Alpine or experimental Debian 13) using PRoot
One-tap installation for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode agents
Persistent background sessions with notification support
Optional USB-based remote access via horus-cli for SSH and port forwarding
Privacy-focused design with no analytics, ads, or required Google services
bestFor: Developers who want to run CLI coding agents from an Android phone or repurpose a spare device as a portable, always-on development box.
notIdealFor: iPhone users, 32-bit or older Android devices, and heavy computational builds requiring desktop-class CPU and memory resources.
recentUpdates: Version 1.2.2 (released 2026-11-18) addressed installation failures and improved error messaging for package management. Version 1.2.1 (2026-11-12) fixed agent install issues on Android 13, and version 1.2.0 (2026-11-07) added copy-to-clipboard functionality and improved terminal UX.
verdict: A polished, privacy-minded way to carry real Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions on an Android phone without rooting it.

name: Jules by Google
pricingDetail: Jules has been read-only since November 11, 2026, and shuts down on December 31, 2026; new tasks cannot be created. It was previously free with a daily task limit and included in Google AI Pro and Ultra. Historical plan prices are no longer an available purchase offer.
description: Jules is an autonomous coding agent designed to handle background development tasks such as bug fixing, dependency upgrades, and test generation. It operates by cloning your GitHub repository into a secure virtual machine to execute plans and open pull requests, allowing developers to delegate repetitive work asynchronously.
keyFeatures: Autonomous asynchronous task execution in cloud VMs
Automatic CI failure detection and resolution via CI Fixer
GitHub integration with automated pull request creation
Support for MCP servers to connect external tools
Proactive task suggestions based on repository scanning
bestFor: Existing Jules users reviewing past sessions and exporting their data before the December 31, 2026 shutdown.
notIdealFor: New tasks of any kind: Jules has been read-only since November 11, 2026.
recentUpdates: On October 29, 2026, Google announced that Jules will be wound down on December 31, 2026, with the service becoming read-only after November 11, 2026.
verdict: Jules is a highly effective tool for automating maintenance and backlog tasks, but it is being discontinued at the end of 2026 as its agentic technology transitions into other platforms like Google Antigravity.

name: OpenHands
pricingDetail: OpenHands is available as a free, open-source version for local use with your own LLM keys. OpenHands Cloud offers a $20/month subscription model for hosted access, with pay-as-you-go model pricing. Enterprise plans are available for self-hosted, multi-user deployments.
description: OpenHands is an open-source platform for autonomous software engineering agents that can interact with repositories, manage development workflows, and execute code. It provides a web-based control center called Agent Canvas, an SDK, and various backend options to run agents locally, in the cloud, or on private infrastructure.
keyFeatures: Optional Docker sandbox isolation for agent execution; the basic local install can run without a sandbox, directly on the host
Model-agnostic support for LLMs like Claude, Codex, and Gemini
Agent Canvas interface for managing workflows and conversations
Automations for Slack, GitHub, Jira, and Linear integration
Self-hosted, Cloud, and Enterprise deployment options
bestFor: Individual developers and teams who require autonomous coding assistance while keeping their proprietary code on their own infrastructure.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer simple editor-based autocomplete or those who are uncomfortable managing infrastructure, as self-hosting requires operational maintenance.
recentUpdates: Version 1.36.0, released on 2026-11-05, introduced significant updates to automation templates, repository pickers for Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, and improved onboarding workflows for self-hosted instances.
verdict: A powerful, highly flexible agentic platform that effectively bridges the gap between local, self-hosted, and cloud-based AI development, suitable for both solo developers and enterprises needing secure automation.

name: SWE-agent
company: Princeton University (in collaboration with Stanford University)
pricingDetail: The tool is available as open-source software; users are responsible for the costs associated with the language model APIs used for execution.
description: SWE-agent is a research-oriented autonomous system that turns language models into software engineering agents capable of fixing issues in GitHub repositories. It uses a custom Agent-Computer Interface to interact with code and environments, logging full trajectories for research and auditing.
keyFeatures: Agent-Computer Interface for file navigation and editing
Full trajectory logging for research and auditability
Docker-sandboxed execution for secure tool interaction
Configuration via a single YAML file
EnIGMA mode for offensive cybersecurity and CTF challenges
bestFor: ML researchers studying agent behavior, academics benchmarking agent performance on SWE-bench, and security researchers performing offensive CTF tasks.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring a managed SaaS product, beginners seeking a GUI or IDE plugin, or users looking for actively developed features, as the project is in maintenance mode.
recentUpdates: Version 1.1.0 (May 22, 2025) introduced SWE-smith support, multilingual evaluation, and various performance fixes.
verdict: While historically significant for introducing the Agent-Computer Interface, SWE-agent has been superseded by mini-swe-agent, which offers similar performance with a simpler and more flexible architecture.

name: mini-swe-agent
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the MIT License; you pay only for the model API calls (via litellm, OpenRouter, Portkey or a local model) and any sandbox infrastructure you run it in.
description: mini-swe-agent is a minimal, open-source AI software engineering agent designed for transparency and research-grade benchmarking. It features a simplified architecture consisting of roughly 100 lines of code that utilizes bash as its sole tool, allowing for high compatibility across various language models.
keyFeatures: Bash-only tool interface
Linear message history for easy debugging
Support for any model via LiteLLM, OpenRouter, and Portkey
Multiple sandboxing options including Docker, Podman, and Singularity
CLI for interactive use and batch benchmark execution
bestFor: Researchers and engineers requiring a transparent, hackable baseline for benchmarking, RL, or fine-tuning pipelines.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a polished, out-of-the-box product with IDE integration, managed support, or comprehensive built-in tooling.
recentUpdates: Version 2.4.6 was released on 2026-07-23, introducing native tool-calling support and multimodal input capabilities.
verdict: The reference minimal coding agent: tiny, model agnostic and benchmark proven, best as a hackable baseline rather than a full daily driver.

name: Sweep
pricingDetail: Offers a free trial with 1,000 autocompletes and $5 in API credits. Paid individual plans include Basic ($10/mo), Pro ($20/mo), and Ultra ($60/mo), which provide unlimited autocomplete and equivalent monthly API credits. Team plans provide $40 per seat in API credits, with additional usage billed on a pay-as-you-go basis (LLM cost plus a 5% markup).
description: Sweep is an AI-powered coding assistant built specifically for JetBrains IDEs that combines predictive next-edit autocomplete with an autonomous agent for repository-wide tasks. It leverages custom models and third-party LLMs to provide context-aware code generation while maintaining a zero-data-retention privacy policy.
keyFeatures: Next-edit autocomplete with custom Tab model
Autonomous agent for multi-file code changes
Repository indexing for context-aware suggestions
Checkpointing and rollback functionality
Support for Remote MCP servers with OAuth 2.0/2.1
bestFor: Individual developers and teams working primarily within JetBrains IDEs who require a native-feeling assistant for routine coding tasks and bug fixes.
notIdealFor: Mixed-editor teams requiring support outside the JetBrains ecosystem, developers needing local self-hosting, or organizations with strict data residency requirements.
recentUpdates: As of early 2026, updates included background bash tool execution, improved agent autocomplete, and enhanced support for Remote MCP servers with OAuth 2.0/2.1 integration.
verdict: Sweep is a highly capable JetBrains-native coding assistant that excels at routine in-IDE tasks and bug fixing, though it lacks the broad cross-editor reach and architectural depth required for complex systems engineering.

name: Ellipsis
pricingDetail: Usage-based billing via prepaid credits for tokens and compute; includes a 10% platform fee. Enterprise support packages are available starting at $5,000 per month.
description: Ellipsis is an agentic platform that provides the infrastructure to deploy, manage, and govern coding agents. It supports a variety of agents and models in sandboxed cloud environments with built-in observability, budget controls, and permission management.
keyFeatures: Model agnostic platform supporting Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and others
Usage-based infrastructure with per-session budget caps and spend limits
Event-driven triggers from Slack, GitHub, Linear, Sentry, and cron schedules
Deployment options in managed Ellipsis cloud or user-owned AWS VPC
Full observability with session transcripts, log history, and fine-grained permissions
bestFor: Teams looking to run custom or existing coding agents reliably in the background with strict security, budget governance, and audit trails.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a simple, out-of-the-box, install-and-forget AI pull request reviewer, as the platform now requires configuring agents and environments via YAML.
recentUpdates: Launched the Ellipsis Agent Cloud on July 28, 2026, pivoting the product from a static code review bot to a comprehensive management platform for coding agents.
verdict: A robust, enterprise-ready platform that effectively moves AI coding agents from local laptops to a governed cloud environment, prioritizing security and reproducibility.

name: Cosine
pricingDetail: Offers a free plan with an 80-task limit. Paid subscription plans include Starter ($19/month), Builder ($49/month), Team ($99/month), Scale ($199/month), and Professional ($999/month), all based on monthly Cosine Credit allocations for task execution. Enterprise pricing is custom.
description: Genie is an autonomous AI software engineering agent designed to perform complex, background coding tasks like refactoring, migrations, and bug fixes. It integrates into team workflows by retrieving context, planning solutions, and submitting pull requests for human review, functioning as an asynchronous team member rather than a real-time IDE assistant.
keyFeatures: Autonomous agent loop for planning, coding, and testing
Full codebase awareness for refactoring and migrations
Parallel execution across multiple isolated worktrees
Deployment flexibility including cloud, VPC, and air-gapped on-premise
Approval-gated actions for secure code submission
bestFor: Engineering teams managing long-lived, complex, or legacy codebases that require autonomous refactoring and large-scale migrations in high-security environments.
notIdealFor: Teams focused on greenfield projects, users requiring IDE-integrated assistants, or organizations heavily dependent on Slack, Jira, or Notion integrations that are not yet natively supported.
recentUpdates: The company has rebranded its core model family to Lumen, with Genie serving as a legacy brand identifier for the platform's autonomous engineering agent.
verdict: A powerful, agentic platform that excels at handling heavy-duty, repetitive engineering workflows asynchronously, though it requires disciplined human review for its parallelized outputs.

name: OpenYak
pricingDetail: OpenYak is free and open-source. It does not resell model access or charge a subscription fee; users connect their own API keys from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, or OpenRouter, use their existing ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Team subscriptions, or run local models via Ollama or Rapid-MLX.
description: OpenYak is a local-first desktop AI agent designed to operate within your local file system, native desktop applications, and web browsers. It provides a visual interface for managing agent tasks, offering transparency and control by allowing users to bring their own model providers or run models locally.
keyFeatures: Native Computer and Browser workspaces with shared human-agent control
Local-first architecture keeping files and memory on your machine
Support for 20+ model providers and local models via Ollama or Rapid-MLX
46+ pre-configured MCP connectors
Built-in channel runtime for messaging platforms like Slack, Discord, and Telegram
bestFor: Local-first teams and power users who need to automate complex workflows across local files, desktop applications, and web browsers while maintaining data privacy.
notIdealFor: Users looking for a hosted web chatbot skin or those requiring cloud-managed, multi-device sync for sensitive AI workspace contexts.
recentUpdates: Version 1.5.0-rc.3 introduced focused Computer and Browser workspaces that pin live views beside the conversation for better task management.
verdict: OpenYak is a highly capable, privacy-focused alternative to platform-locked AI agents, offering significant transparency and control for desktop-based automation tasks.

name: DeepAgents JS
pricingDetail: The software is 100% open source and distributed under the MIT license.
description: DeepAgents JS is an opinionated agent harness designed for complex, long-running, and multi-step tasks. It provides a batteries-included environment with built-in planning, filesystem management, and sub-agent orchestration on top of LangGraph.
keyFeatures: Autonomous planning and sub-agent delegation
Virtual filesystem with pluggable backends and permission controls
Context management including summarization and prompt caching
Human-in-the-loop support for runtime approval
Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for tool connectivity
bestFor: Complex, non-deterministic, and long-running multi-step tasks that benefit from autonomous planning and isolated sub-agent execution.
notIdealFor: Simple, single-step tasks or scenarios where maintaining full, non-compressed intermediate context is required.
recentUpdates: As of November 24, 2026, version 0.1.2 was released, introducing on-demand MCP tool discovery, message support for local sessions (Claude Code/dcode), and support for confidential OAuth clients for MCP servers.
verdict: A robust, highly flexible framework for developers needing to build sophisticated, multi-agent systems with infrastructure independence and fine-grained control over execution flow.

name: Orkas
pricingDetail: The desktop app is free and includes 500 bonus credits for managed models; paid plans (Lite, Pro, Max) starting at $11.99/month provide increased cloud storage, more shared projects, multi-device sync, and monthly credit allowances.
description: Orkas is an open-source, local-first multi-agent AI desktop client that coordinates specialist agents to handle complex, recurring workflows. It allows users to manage projects, automate tasks with a Commander agent, and maintain data privacy by keeping files and keys on the user's machine.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent orchestration with a Commander agent
Local-first architecture with optional cloud sync
Scheduled automations and auto-advance task workflows
Support for custom agents and third-party tools like Claude Code and Codex
Integrated web app publishing for collaborative projects
bestFor: Professionals and small teams needing to automate complex, multi-step business processes that require memory, context, and coordination across different specialist roles.
notIdealFor: Users looking for a simple, all-purpose chatbot for one-off queries or those seeking a pure code library to embed into another application.
recentUpdates: The v2026.11.16 release added features for content workbench and product listing apps, improved video timeline controls, and enhanced inspection and export tools for various document formats.
verdict: A powerful, private-by-default desktop client that transforms AI from a simple chat interface into a project-based autonomous team, ideal for professionals managing long-term business processes.

name: Kody
pricingDetail: Offers a Free tier with volume caps and a Pro plan at $12/month or $120/year, with additional prepaid credits available for high-volume needs.
description: Kody is an autonomous and asynchronous cloud-based software factory that provides AI agents with persistent memory, secure credential storage, and a server-side execution environment. It allows agents to save, schedule, and run tasks independently of any specific chat interface or active local session.
keyFeatures: Durable state management for agent memory
Secure credential and API key storage
Server-side execution for scheduled jobs and webhooks
Reusable code packages for agent-authored tasks
MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for interoperability
bestFor: Developers who want to provide their AI agents with long-term memory, secure API access, and the ability to run automated workflows in the background.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a standalone chat interface, a replacement for AI models like Claude or ChatGPT, or those requiring a frozen, auditable tool catalog for security reviews.
recentUpdates: Kody v2026.11.24 introduced an organization referral program. Recent preceding updates added Kody Desktop for Windows and Linux, a command menu (Cmd+K), per-person access pages, and advanced execution contexts.
verdict: Kody is a powerful infrastructure layer that successfully turns ephemeral AI interactions into reliable, persistent software automations, making it an essential utility for power users of AI agents.

name: Omnigent
pricingDetail: Omnigent is open-source (Apache 2.0). It requires users to bring their own API keys, model subscriptions (e.g., Claude Pro, ChatGPT), or compatible gateways.
description: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that provides a unified orchestration layer for managing, monitoring, and collaborating with various AI coding agents. It enables users to enforce security policies, implement cost controls, and run agents within secure local or cloud sandboxes across multiple devices.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom YAML agents
Stateful, data-centric governance policies for cost capping and tool access control
Secure sandboxing with support for local OS, AWS Lambda, and various cloud providers
Real-time collaboration via shareable session URLs across terminal, web, and desktop
Automated triggers for workflows via Jira, Slack, GitHub, Linear, and PagerDuty
bestFor: Platform and DevOps teams managing multiple coding agents who require centralized policy enforcement, spend tracking, and collaborative session reviews.
notIdealFor: Non-technical users seeking a point-and-click agent product, users requiring a fully managed service, or single-agent workflows where the infrastructure overhead outweighs the orchestration benefits.
recentUpdates: Version 0.23.0 introduced improved automation controls, session grids for multi-agent monitoring, /rewind for chat history, and enhanced inline PR review tools. Version 0.22.0 added support for event-based triggers (Jira, Slack, GitHub, etc.), native desktop shortcuts, and AWS Lambda MicroVM sandboxes.
verdict: A powerful, governance-focused orchestration tool that is best suited for teams who need to standardize and secure multiple agent workflows but are comfortable managing their own infrastructure.

name: Manus
pricingDetail: Offers a Free plan, Pro plans starting at $20/month or $40/month, and a Team plan starting at $20 per seat/month. Includes optional credit add-ons.
description: Manus is an autonomous AI agent platform that utilizes a virtual computer to plan, research, write code, and execute complex workflows. The system features a workspace for local file interaction and supports asynchronous cloud execution, allowing tasks to continue after the user leaves the application.
keyFeatures: Cascade engine for connected project workflows
Manus Studio for local and cloud-based file manipulation
Automations for scheduled or triggered multi-step tasks
Cue for managing teams of autonomous agents with individual identities
Integrated video and game development tools
bestFor: Open-ended, multi-step research tasks, long-running data aggregation, and autonomous content generation that requires multiple iterations.
notIdealFor: Highly sensitive data, coding or debugging within complex existing codebases, and tasks on websites frequently protected by paywalls or CAPTCHAs.
recentUpdates: Launched Manus 2.0 on October 1, 2026, featuring the Cascade internal engine, Manus Studio, Video Editor, Game Dev, Cloud Computer, Remote Control, Automations, and the Cue personal agent application.
verdict: Manus is a powerful, highly autonomous agent platform that excels at bridging the gap between digital planning and final output delivery, particularly for technical and creative project workflows.

name: LoopTroop
pricingDetail: LoopTroop is free and fully open-source, though users are responsible for their own AI model provider API costs.
description: LoopTroop is a local GUI orchestrator for long-running, high-correctness AI software delivery that manages the entire lifecycle from idea to merged code. It utilizes a multi-model LLM council, isolated Git worktrees, and automated recovery loops to maintain code quality during complex, multi-file development tasks.
keyFeatures: Multi-model LLM Council for anonymous planning and voting
Isolated execution beads using Git worktrees
Ralph-style recovery loops for unattended error handling
Precise context engineering to prevent AI drift
Integrated AI chat assistant with project-wide awareness
bestFor: Complex, mid-size to large feature work requiring high correctness and reliable, long-running unattended execution.
notIdealFor: Quick one-shot edits, trivial fixes, or chat-first exploratory coding where planning overhead introduces unnecessary latency.
recentUpdates: Version 0.6.4 improved responsiveness, startup speed, and logging performance; version 0.6.3 refined error handling and safety scans; version 0.6.2 introduced an integrated AI chat assistant and improved retry logic.
verdict: LoopTroop is an excellent, sophisticated tool for developers who prioritize accuracy and transparent automation over speed. It successfully solves common AI coding issues like context drift and model bias by treating tasks as formal, recoverable state machines rather than simple chat conversations.

name: Muse
pricingDetail: Free for standard usage, with a Power plan at $20/month (500M tokens/week) and a Maximum plan at $100/month (3B tokens/week).
description: Muse is a personal AI agent from Meta that executes tasks, manages goals, and automates workflows by interacting with your apps and services. It operates within a persistent, isolated secure virtual machine to handle complex requests, browse the web, and build its own tools under your direction.
keyFeatures: Secure virtual machine for isolated task execution
Multi-step goal planning and background execution
Integrations with apps like Shopify, Slack, Notion, and Meta ad tools
Human-in-the-loop approvals for sensitive actions
Artifact generation including documents, code, and dashboards
bestFor: Individuals and small businesses needing to automate cross-platform tasks, manage marketing workflows, or juggle long-running personal to-do lists.
notIdealFor: Regulated industries handling sensitive health or financial data, or organizations requiring strict enterprise-level admin controls and audit logs.
recentUpdates: On November 5, 2026, voice conversations and expressive avatars were released. On September 29, 2026, Muse for Small Business added integrations for Facebook Pages, Shopify, and QuickBooks.
verdict: Muse represents a transition from chatbot to agent, excelling at managing complex, long-running goals, though it currently requires significant initial setup and supervision for basic transactional tasks.

name: OtoDock
pricingDetail: Free for self-hosting up to 5 users. Growing teams license by seats starting at 25 EUR/month (4-15 users), with higher tiers available for larger organizations. All features are included in every tier.
description: OtoDock is a self-hosted platform for deploying teams of autonomous AI agents that run on your own infrastructure and AI subscriptions. It uses a security-focused architecture with kernel sandboxing and network isolation to manage agent tasks, collaborations, and workflows securely.
keyFeatures: Multi-tenant agent collaboration with departments and delegation
Self-hosted infrastructure with kernel-level sandboxing and network isolation
Support for Claude Code, Codex, and local LLMs via Ollama or OpenAI-compatible servers
Automated workflows including scheduled tasks, webhooks, and persistent memory
Integrated phone support, document editing, and remote machine control
bestFor: Small teams, technical founders, and privacy-conscious organizations that require sandboxed, self-hosted AI agents and are comfortable managing a Docker-based server stack.
notIdealFor: Teams seeking a zero-ops managed SaaS, non-technical users, or organizations that lack existing Anthropic or OpenAI subscriptions to bring to the platform.
recentUpdates: Version 1.9.1 (2026-11-04) introduced memory topic limits, refined permissions for agent tasks, enhanced image/media creation capabilities for scheduled tasks, and added the ability to delegate chats to run on local machines.
verdict: OtoDock is a powerful, enterprise-grade platform for teams that prioritize data sovereignty and security, offering a transparent, fair-source approach to complex AI automation.

name: Firstmate
pricingDetail: Free (open source, MIT)
description: Firstmate is an agent distro that coordinates multiple autonomous coding agents by serving as a single liaison for the user. It manages a crew of agents operating in isolated git worktrees and session backends to handle parallel tasks like fixes, investigations, and PR generation.
keyFeatures: Unified liaison for multi-agent supervision
Parallel task execution in isolated git worktrees
Event-driven, zero-token supervision
Support for persistent secondary agents (secondmates)
Restart-proof state management
bestFor: Developers managing multiple parallel coding tasks who want to avoid manual session juggling and require structured, supervised agent workflows.
notIdealFor: Windows users, developers seeking a simple one-click GUI application, or teams requiring strict process-level credential isolation.
recentUpdates: On 2026-10-23, the project announced full support for the Rex runtime backend.
verdict: A robust, highly disciplined orchestration layer that effectively transforms general-purpose coding agents into a coordinated crew, though it requires a significant learning curve and specific terminal infrastructure.

name: OpenResearch
pricingDetail: The tool is open-source and free to self-host. An optional hosted compute marketplace is available on a metered, prepaid, usage-based basis, passing through provider costs directly with no OpenResearch markup.
description: OpenResearch is an open-source research agent harness that integrates with existing coding agents to manage literature review, hypothesis development, and experiment execution. It functions as a local-first workspace that records research artifacts and logs in a SQL database to help agents learn from past results.
keyFeatures: Native support for coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor
Integration with research databases including alphaXiv, OpenAlex, bioRxiv, and PubMed
Local experimentation engine that tracks experiments, logs, and metrics in a git-based structure
Support for local model inference and various compute backends like SSH, Slurm, Kubernetes, and managed GPUs
Local-first architecture that keeps research artifacts and conversations on the user's machine
bestFor: Researchers and developers who need to automate scientific workflows, literature reviews, and experiment iteration using their existing AI coding agents.
notIdealFor: Users who do not have an existing coding agent subscription or API key, or those requiring a closed-source managed SaaS platform that handles data storage centrally.
recentUpdates: On November 20, 2026, the team introduced the OpenResearch Intelligence Index to track autoresearch capabilities. The v0.2.18 release (October 9, 2026) included improvements to the project run command, Modal environment builds, terminal socket handling, and artifact rendering.
verdict: A powerful, high-velocity, open-source tool for researchers who prefer a local-first environment and want to treat experiment logs and code as primary, version-controlled research artifacts.

name: Coder
pricingDetail: Offers a free open-source Community edition, a paid Premium tier for enterprises, and a custom AI Premium tier for organizations scaling AI-native workflows.
description: Coder is a self-hosted platform for providing governed cloud development environments and AI coding agents on your own infrastructure. It centralizes control over workspace provisioning, security policies, and AI agent execution, enabling organizations to run code and agentic workflows in air-gapped or network-isolated environments.
keyFeatures: Fully self-hosted AI agent loop running in the control plane
Agentic workflow orchestration via chat interface and API
Centralized governance for models, prompts, and cost tracking
No API keys or agent software required inside workspaces
Audit-ready logging for all agent actions and developer activity
bestFor: Regulated industries and enterprises requiring strict control, auditability, and air-gapped capability for their AI coding and development workflows.
notIdealFor: Small teams, individual developers, or organizations lacking the infrastructure engineering capacity to host and maintain their own control plane and workspace templates.
recentUpdates: On September 9, 2026, Coder announced the general availability of Coder Agents, introducing a fully self-hosted, air-gap-capable agentic experience that integrates directly into the Coder control plane.
verdict: Coder is a robust, security-focused infrastructure platform that allows organizations to deploy agentic coding workflows without compromising data privacy or administrative control.

name: AX (Agent Executor)
pricingDetail: Free (Apache License 2.0). Users are responsible for infrastructure costs including Kubernetes cluster resources, storage, and model API usage.
description: AX is a declarative, open-source orchestration runtime designed to run and manage large-scale autonomous agent workloads within Kubernetes clusters. It provides primitives to handle isolated sandboxed execution, workspace management, and task suspension for optimized resource utilization.
keyFeatures: Isolated sandboxed execution with resource and network limits
Declarative Kubernetes-style API (Task, Workspace, Model)
Efficient task suspension and resumption to checkpoint state
Interactive debugging tools like ax ssh
High-throughput architecture for managing large agent fleets
bestFor: Enterprises and platform teams managing large-scale, bursty, or long-running fleets of autonomous agents that require infrastructure-level governance.
notIdealFor: Small teams or individual developers seeking a quick-start framework, or production environments requiring immediate security hardening, as the tool is currently in early-stage development with significant operational overhead.
recentUpdates: Version v0.4.0-rc.1 was released on November 20, 2026, introducing features like improved resource name validation and backend storage transitions to Postgres, following the v0.3.1 release on September 25, 2026.
verdict: AX is a powerful, architectural blueprint for fleet-scale agent orchestration that offers significant control and scalability, but it is currently highly experimental and requires expert operational knowledge to maintain.

name: Agent Substrate
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the Apache License 2.0; you pay for your own Kubernetes cluster, compute, storage and model usage.
description: Agent Substrate is a secure-by-default, low-latency execution runtime designed to run millions of stateful, autonomous agent sandboxes on Kubernetes. It optimizes resource usage by decoupling stateful agents from compute resources, allowing idle agents to be snapshotted to storage and resumed on pre-warmed worker nodes in under 500 milliseconds.
keyFeatures: Stateful snapshotting and rapid resume under 500ms
Zero-trust isolation using gVisor or microVMs
Per-agent cryptographic identity via SPIFFE
Credential injection via egress gateway
High-density execution with 10x higher capacity than standard containers
bestFor: Large-scale platforms running thousands to millions of mostly-idle, stateful autonomous agents, such as productivity assistants or coding environments.
notIdealFor: Small teams with few agents where standard sandboxing solutions are sufficient, or workloads requiring persistent open network connections like long-lived database sessions.
recentUpdates: The project reached version 1.0 and was donated to the CNCF (Sandbox level) in September 2026. General availability for Agent Substrate on GKE was announced on November 5, 2026, alongside new router parking features and per-container limits.
verdict: A serious, production-minded isolation layer for agent fleets; heavy to operate, but one of the strongest open options for running untrusted agents at scale.

name: Rivet
pricingDetail: Open-source (Apache-2.0) and free to run locally or self-host, with S3 as the only dependency. Rivet Cloud (fully managed dedicated clusters on AWS or GCP) and BYOC (control plane in your own VPC, managed by Rivet) are managed options; see rivet.dev for their pricing.
description: Rivet is an open-source platform for building and scaling agentic workloads using the actor model. It provides durable, lightweight actors that run inside your own backend, featuring persistent state, SQLite databases, and low-latency cold starts.
keyFeatures: Durable Actors with persistent SQLite storage backed by S3
Single stateless binary architecture
Lightweight sandboxing and isolated execution
Fault-tolerant scheduling with automatic state recovery
WebSocket and HTTP networking support
bestFor: Developers building long-lived, stateful AI agents, collaborative editing, or multi-step agentic workflows that require durability across restarts.
notIdealFor: Simple, one-shot scheduled tasks or repository-level maintenance chores where an agent does not need long-term persistent memory.
recentUpdates: Released Rivet 3.0 Preview featuring the WarpDrive storage engine (2026-10-26), added Actor Forking for SQLite (2026-11-11), and announced Alchemy support for self-hosting (2026-11-24).
verdict: A well-engineered, actively shipped runtime that moves the agent loop out of the sandbox; strongest for TypeScript teams building agent products, less relevant if you only consume coding agents.

name: GitHub Agentic Workflows
pricingDetail: The gh-aw tool is free and open-source. Users pay only for GitHub Actions compute minutes and the standard inference rates charged by their chosen AI engine provider (or consume their existing Copilot quota).
description: GitHub Agentic Workflows is an open-source project from GitHub Next that enables developers to define AI-powered repository automation using natural language in Markdown files. These workflows are compiled into standard GitHub Actions, allowing coding agents to handle reasoning-based tasks like issue triage, code review, and documentation maintenance within secure, sandboxed environments.
keyFeatures: Natural language workflow definition using Markdown with YAML frontmatter
Layered security with sandboxed execution, read-only default permissions, and threat detection
Integration with multiple AI engines including GitHub Copilot, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex, and Google Gemini
Built-in budget and usage controls via AI Credits (1 AIC = $0.01 USD)
Workflow compilation into standard GitHub Actions YAML
bestFor: Tasks requiring reasoning or interpretation, such as issue triage, PR review, CI failure analysis, dependency management, and generating repository reports.
notIdealFor: Deterministic, repetitive tasks like standard builds, testing, linting, or deployments where fixed scripts are more reliable and cost-effective.
recentUpdates: Achieved general availability on October 28, 2026, introducing ARC and Docker-in-Docker support, production-ready budget forecasting via 'gh aw forecast', and improved model routing options.
verdict: An effective, secure way to extend GitHub Actions with AI reasoning that prioritizes safety through guardrails and human review, though it requires careful cost management and is not a replacement for traditional, deterministic CI/CD pipelines.

name: Strands Harness SDK
pricingDetail: The project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 license and is free to use.
description: Strands Agents is an open-source SDK for building and running AI agents in Python and TypeScript. It provides a model-agnostic framework for orchestrating agent loops, memory, tool integration, and multi-agent patterns in production environments.
keyFeatures: Model-agnostic support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, and Ollama
Pre-assembled 'Strands harness' for production-ready agent deployments
Multi-agent patterns including Swarm, Graph, and agent-to-agent communication
Automatic context management including prompt caching, truncation, and summarization
Native integration with MCP servers and custom tools
bestFor: Developers who need a production-grade, end-to-end agent harness that provides full control over execution, orchestration, and observability without being locked into a specific model provider.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring a simple, no-code interface or users who prefer a managed, all-in-one SaaS platform that handles token costs and hosting rather than a self-hosted SDK approach.
recentUpdates: On November 4, 2026, the SDK added expanded built-in tools for file management, web fetching, and multi-agent delegation, deprecating legacy tool packages. On October 30, 2026, version 1.23.0 for TypeScript was released, introducing new persistence strategies, limit controls for multi-agent graphs, and enhanced model capability reporting.
verdict: A robust, developer-first toolkit that successfully balances the flexibility of a low-level SDK with the practical convenience of the pre-assembled Strands harness for production deployments.

name: Paperclip
pricingDetail: Open-source and free to self-host under an MIT license. Cloud-hosted plans are available for 10 EUR/month or 100 EUR/year with a 7-day trial.
description: Paperclip is an open-source, self-hosted control plane that allows teams to manage and orchestrate multiple AI agents from a single web interface. It provides a structured environment for AI work by incorporating organizational hierarchies, task management, approval gates, and budget enforcement.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent orchestration and org-chart management
Task-based workflow with built-in review and approval stages
Hard-stop budget enforcement at company, project, and agent levels
Support for various runtimes including Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI
Self-hosted infrastructure with local database and encrypted secret storage
bestFor: Teams running multiple AI agents that require collaborative task management, spending guardrails, and human-in-the-loop oversight.
notIdealFor: Individuals running a single agent in a local terminal or developers seeking a turn-key autonomous business platform without setup or oversight.
recentUpdates: Version 2026.1117.0 (November 17, 2026) made the Coordinator layout and Agent Chat the default workspace, with task chat showing a Runner agent's plan, inline diffs, tool calls and subagents. Version 2026.1106.0 (November 6, 2026) made the Paperclip Runner the default for new agents and added GitHub Copilot as a native harness.
verdict: A sophisticated and highly structured approach to agent management that treats AI like headcount rather than code, making it the premier choice for organizations needing professional-grade auditability and governance.

name: OpenSRE
pricingDetail: OpenSRE is an open-source project licensed under the Apache 2.0 license. It is free to use, though users are responsible for their own LLM API costs or self-hosted model infrastructure.
description: OpenSRE is an open-source, self-hosted AI agent designed to improve CI/CD reliability and automate production incident investigation. It analyzes logs, traces, and metrics from over 60 integrated tools to diagnose issues and proactively push fixes to pull requests.
keyFeatures: Autonomous root cause analysis for CI/CD failures and production incidents
Evidence-backed remediation with automated pull request fix generation
Deep integration with 60+ observability, cloud, and incident management tools
Interactive terminal-based shell for natural language operations
Flexible deployment via local CLI, self-hosted containers, or managed gateway
bestFor: SRE teams and engineers looking to automate incident response and CI/CD reliability tasks while maintaining full control over their infrastructure and data.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a zero-configuration, fully managed SaaS platform, as the tool is heavily optimized for CLI control and self-hosted, evidence-based operations.
recentUpdates: Recent updates in November 2026 include the introduction of official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server presets for platforms like Grafana, Datadog, and AWS, alongside bridge capabilities for Sentry and PostHog. October and November releases also refined CLI security, improved GitHub authentication, and added database observability integrations.
