verdict: OpenSRE is a powerful and highly extensible framework that offers deep transparency and custom control, making it an excellent choice for teams that prioritize privacy and want an auditable, self-hosted AI pipeline for production operations.

name: SuperPlane
pricingDetail: Offers a pay-as-you-go model with no monthly fee, a Starter plan at $20/organization/month, a Team plan at $50/user/month, and a custom Enterprise plan. Usage costs for sandbox time and models apply, with 10% markup on SuperPlane-provided model tokens.
description: SuperPlane is an open-source software factory designed to automate routine engineering tasks by coordinating coding agents from ticket intake to verified, merge-ready pull requests. It provides a standardized, observable workflow that sits around existing tools to handle implementation, testing, and feedback loops while keeping human developers in control of final decisions.
keyFeatures: Automated ticket intake with confidence scoring
Parallel task execution in isolated cloud development environments
Continuous feedback loops for failed CI checks or review feedback
Integration with over 400 engineering tools and platforms
Workflow guardrails that enforce team standards consistently
bestFor: Engineering teams looking to automate routine maintenance, bug fixes, dependency updates, and paper cuts to free up developers for higher-level work.
notIdealFor: Highly ambiguous or complex tasks that require significant human judgment, scope definition, or trade-off analysis that cannot be bounded or verified.
recentUpdates: Launched version 1.0 on October 27, 2026, establishing it as an open-source, model-agnostic software factory. Earlier in July 2026, version 0.30.0 introduced a factory-first onboarding flow, Linear integration, and expanded GitLab support.
verdict: SuperPlane effectively bridges the gap between raw AI agents and production-ready engineering workflows by providing a structured, repeatable, and observable automation factory.

name: Docker Agent
pricingDetail: Free (Open Source, Apache 2.0 license). Users pay only for third-party AI model usage via their selected providers; local models via Docker Model Runner or Ollama have no API cost.
description: Docker Agent is a declarative framework that enables developers to build, run, and share AI agent teams using YAML or HCL configuration files. It acts as a portable runtime that manages multi-agent orchestration, tool execution, and OCI-compliant distribution without requiring custom application code.
keyFeatures: Declarative multi-agent orchestration via YAML/HCL
Model-agnostic design supporting cloud providers and local models
OCI registry support for packaging and sharing agents as artifacts
Extensive tool ecosystem via built-in tools and MCP servers
Flexible execution modes including TUI, headless CLI, HTTP API, and A2A protocol
bestFor: Developers and platform engineers who need to standardize, version, and share specialized AI agent teams for tasks like automated coding, SRE incident triage, or data research.
notIdealFor: Teams that prefer defining agent logic in code (Python/TypeScript), those seeking a pre-built SaaS product, or organizations requiring a slow-moving, stable configuration surface.
recentUpdates: As of November 2026, version 1.154.0 added credential-based selection and discovery for Lunaroute and improved sandbox compatibility. Previous updates introduced hook-driven agent routing, a debug tool command, and the ability to load skills directly from GitHub repositories.
verdict: A powerful, workflow-centric tool that applies container-like portability to AI agents, making it an excellent choice for teams that want to treat agent configurations as versioned, sharable infrastructure.

name: Orbi
pricingDetail: Self-hosted Orbi is free under AGPL-3.0 or the Sustainable Use License, requiring user-provided API keys. Orbi Cloud offers a trial of 3 successful merged deliveries, with paid plans Solo ($29/month, 400M tokens) and Pro ($79/month, 1.2B tokens).
description: Orbi is an autonomous, open-source AI coding agent that transforms GitHub Issues into reviewed, merged code and tagged releases. It operates by separating implementation and review into two independent AI sessions to ensure delivery quality before finalizing merges.
keyFeatures: Independent AI review and repair cycle for pull requests
GitHub Issue-to-tagged-release automation
Self-hosted or cloud-managed infrastructure
Bring-your-own-model support for self-hosted instances
Automated splitting of complex requests into individual Issues
bestFor: Automating software delivery workflows where repository maintenance involves repetitive tasks, testing, and merging issues according to defined acceptance criteria.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring complex human creative oversight for every code change or scenarios where CI/test suites are non-existent or unreliable.
recentUpdates: Recent updates include the addition of a feature to split large requests into multiple Issues and the refinement of the harness for reliable code generation based on over 1,500 measured deliveries.
verdict: Orbi is a robust, production-focused coding agent that excels at end-to-end automation by separating the roles of implementer and reviewer within a CI-integrated workflow.

name: Reason
pricingDetail: Offers a free peer-to-peer Reason Network for agent communication; paid plans are available for cloud-based sessions, enterprise use, and specific professional tiers like Pro, Pro+, and Ultra.
description: Reason is an autonomous software engineering agent that works across your tools to handle tasks from start to finish, such as fixing bugs, opening pull requests, and managing recurring operational workflows. It utilizes a custom harness to optimize token usage and cost efficiency while operating within isolated cloud environments.
keyFeatures: Autonomous cloud-based agents with terminal and browser access
Parallel tool execution via a JavaScript-based codemode
Support for Loops to trigger work on schedules or events
Extensive integrations with Slack, GitHub, Stripe, PostHog, and Google Workspace
Shareable agents with custom instructions and memory
bestFor: Standing, recurring jobs that span multiple tools, such as engineering bug fixes, finance reporting, or marketing site updates.
notIdealFor: High-stakes decision making, roles requiring human-equivalent help desk/CRM functionality, or tasks needing a dedicated mailbox or voice features.
recentUpdates: Recent updates include support for GPT-6.2 (Astra/Sol) and Gemini 4 (Neon/Carbon/Hydrogen) models in preview, MAI Code 2 for GitHub Copilot, and an expanded iPhone app with file management and pull request review capabilities.
verdict: A highly efficient, model-agnostic coding harness that excels at reducing agent overhead and fostering a connected ecosystem of AI coding tools.

name: Rakazo
pricingDetail: Rakazo offers a free trial period on its hosted platform. Paid plans are available via Stripe, which can include model credits or an own-key model plan. Self-hosted deployments are free to use but require users to pay their own model providers.
description: Rakazo is an open-source platform for persistent, autonomous AI agents that feature their own memory, routines, and dedicated virtual computers. It allows users to connect their preferred AI models to handle recurring tasks like inbox management, sales outreach, and coding autonomously.
keyFeatures: Dedicated virtual computers for each bot with browser and terminal access
Support for custom AI models via API keys, subscriptions, or local runners
Configurable routines and triggers based on schedules, webhooks, or GitHub events
Human-in-the-loop approval controls for sensitive actions
Multi-agent delegation and group collaboration in chat interfaces
bestFor: Users with recurring, multi-step workflows who want to delegate tasks to always-on agents while maintaining control over their data and model selection.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a simple, free chat-only interface for occasional questions or those wanting an all-in-one assistant without performing any setup or configuration.
recentUpdates: Version 0.8.0 added iPhone/iPad share sheet support, DeepSeek as a default model for self-hosters, and improved group chat dynamics. Version 0.7.0 introduced Pro and Max tiers, multi-organization login, and enhanced security fixes.
verdict: Rakazo is a powerful, highly flexible framework for power users who want deep, autonomous control over AI agents, offering a compelling open-source alternative to proprietary agent platforms.

name: Open-CUAK
pricingDetail: Open-CUAK itself is free and open-source (self-hosted via Homebrew or Docker); Aident's separate hosted platform has a free tier with 300 credits/month and paid plans from $12/mo (Basic) up to $120/mo (Max) billed annually, plus custom Enterprise.
description: Open-CUAK (Open Computer Use Agent Kit) is an open-source, self-hostable platform designed to manage automation agents at scale, particularly for browser-based tasks. It enables users to run vision-based automation locally using various frontier or open-source models while providing tools for secure, isolated browser execution.
keyFeatures: Local execution of vision-based browser automation
Support for multiple frontier and open-source vision models
Isolated remote browser environments for secure task execution
Browser extension for turning browsers into agent-ready companions
Parallel management and deployment of multiple automation agents
bestFor: Developers and technical teams requiring a free, self-hosted, and privacy-focused framework for building browser-based automation agents.
notIdealFor: Non-technical users who need a managed, turnkey SaaS solution that does not require self-hosting or maintenance.
recentUpdates: A new alpha version (v0.0.1-alpha) was released on October 20, 2026.
verdict: Open-CUAK provides a powerful, privacy-oriented framework for building browser-based agents, though it remains a technical tool that requires ongoing maintenance and verification for production use.

name: Omnara
pricingDetail: The Omnara platform itself is free to self-host under an Apache 2.0 license. On Omnara Cloud, there is no platform fee; users can bring their own model keys and machines for free, or pay as you go using Omnara credits for hosted models and sandbox infrastructure.
description: Omnara is an open-source, model-agnostic control plane designed to manage durable AI agents in production. It provides a platform to launch, execute, and monitor agents that survive crashes and disconnects while allowing users to utilize their own models, machines, and infrastructure.
keyFeatures: Durable execution with automatic crash recovery and state persistence in Postgres
Model-agnostic architecture supporting any model provider or self-hosted models
Integrations with Slack, Discord, and GitHub for automated workflows and event handling
Multi-machine support including self-hosted hardware, sandboxes, and cloud-managed pools
Role-based access control with audit logging, secret management, and per-tool permissions
bestFor: Engineering teams and platform builders needing a production-grade durable agent API for internal tools or product integrations who want to avoid vendor lock-in.
notIdealFor: Hobbyists building simple local chatbots or teams already utilizing code-first orchestration libraries like LangGraph who prefer custom Python-based state machine logic.
recentUpdates: October 2026 updates introduced E2B and Superserve sandbox support, scoped Git access for enhanced security, and improved agent dashboarding. September 2026 updates added subagent delegation, Slack/Discord/GitHub integrations, memory stores, and support for models like GPT-6 and Claude Opus 5.5.
verdict: Omnara is a robust, open-source alternative to proprietary managed agent platforms like Claude Managed Agents, offering excellent flexibility for developers who need to integrate AI agents into their own products or internal infrastructure.

name: Scion
pricingDetail: Scion is an open-source orchestration platform; costs are associated with the infrastructure chosen to run it (such as Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, or local compute resources).
description: Scion is an open-source orchestration platform designed for teams to manage AI agents, enabling them to delegate tasks, share findings, and work in parallel. It serves as a hypervisor for agents, providing the necessary messaging, execution environments, and visibility to coordinate complex agentic projects from local workstations to cloud infrastructure.
keyFeatures: Pluggable execution runtimes including Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, and Cloud Run
Support for various AI agent harnesses such as Claude Code and Gemini CLI
Consistent CLI and web dashboard for task delegation and monitoring
Infrastructure-agnostic agent lifecycle management via a centralized Hub
Declarative role-based access control and scoped secrets for multi-user teams
bestFor: Teams requiring a scalable, secure, and durable orchestration layer for AI agents that supports both local workstation development and production-grade, multi-user hosted deployments.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a simple, zero-infrastructure AI chatbot, as Scion requires configuring a Hub and managing containerized runtime environments.
recentUpdates: As of November 11, 2026, version 0.3.0 was released. Recent functional updates include the requirement of a Hub for all agent commands, the introduction of asynchronous agent launch, native Windows client CLI support, and expanded integration with tools like VS Code and SSH.
verdict: Scion is a robust, professional-grade platform for teams serious about managing AI agent lifecycles, offering significant flexibility in how agents are hosted and secured.

name: Cindy
pricingDetail: The Cindy client software is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license. Users can connect their own API keys or existing model subscriptions (such as Claude Code or Codex) at no extra cost to Cindy. Alternatively, Cindy offers an optional managed model service with credit-based pricing tiers: PLUS ($20/mo or $16/mo on a plan), SUPER ($100/mo or $80/mo on a plan), and ULTRA ($200/mo or $160/mo on a plan), with pay-as-you-go top-up options available.
description: Cindy is an open-source, local-first AI agent platform that unifies various agent harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, and Pi into a single cross-device workflow. It allows users to orchestrate complex tasks by connecting their existing model subscriptions, API keys, or using the platform's own managed model service.
keyFeatures: Cross-device synchronization for tasks, files, and conversations
Unified interface for multiple agent harnesses including Claude Code and Codex
Built-in remote desktop access to operate connected computers from mobile
Support for multi-agent workflows with parallel execution and independent review
Customizable companions with persistent memory, skills, and plugin capabilities
bestFor: Developers and power users who need to orchestrate complex, multi-step tasks across different AI models and devices while maintaining persistent project context.
notIdealFor: Users looking for a fully self-hosted backend solution, or those expecting a flat-fee subscription that provides unlimited model usage.
recentUpdates: Recent releases (e.g., v0.1.19) introduced enhanced companion collaboration, improved mobile-to-desktop remote connections, richer message support for charts and interactive controls, and native iOS task options.
verdict: Cindy is a powerful, flexible AI orchestration client that effectively bridges the gap between disparate agent harnesses by centralizing them into a single, continuity-focused workflow.

name: Zozo HQ
pricingDetail: The Local Stack is free for personal use on your own machine. Hosted plans are billed monthly at $40 (Standard), $50 (Plus), and $60 (Pro) depending on resource capacity; there is no markup on model inference costs.
description: Zozo HQ is a managed harness for autonomous coding agents that automates software work by turning GitHub issues or vague ideas into pull requests. It provides a dedicated, persistent environment that continues running tasks even when your local machine is offline.
keyFeatures: Durable, hosted execution environment for coding agents
Intake sessions for refining feature ideas into structured plans
Integration with GitHub, Jira Cloud, and Bitbucket Cloud
Append-only event journals for transparent progress monitoring
Auto-dispatch system for managing task queues and dependency resolution
bestFor: Developers and teams who want to automate backlog management and review agent-authored pull requests without managing the runtime lifecycle manually.
notIdealFor: Users seeking an interactive, chat-based terminal for active pair programming or those requiring integrations beyond GitHub or Jira/Bitbucket.
recentUpdates: v0.43.2 (2026-11-13) improved GitHub token consistency; v0.43.1 (2026-11-12) fixed capacity waitlist grants; v0.43.0 (2026-11-02) introduced project-specific agents, subagent delegation, and card-free hosted stack grants.
verdict: Zozo provides a robust, transparently-priced solution for hands-off project automation, effectively bridging the gap between ideation and pull request submission for those already invested in agent runtimes.

name: Agensh
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the MIT license; users are responsible for the costs of LLM inference for multiple concurrent agents and the required Linux infrastructure.
description: Agensh is a self-organized, multi-agent harness that enables large teams of AI agents to collaborate on coding tasks without a central orchestrator. It uses a shared Gitea workspace, messaging interface, and context mechanism to coordinate up to 1,024 asynchronous agents.
keyFeatures: Decentralized cooperation loop without a central orchestrator
Shared workspace, messaging interface, and context tracking
Support for Copilot, Codex, Claude Code, and Pi backends
Scalable architecture supporting up to 1,024 concurrent agents
Single-node team deployment via Docker Compose
bestFor: Researchers and engineers experimenting with multi-agent coordination patterns or reproducing ProgramBench experiments.
notIdealFor: Developers looking for a turnkey, daily-use coding assistant, as it requires significant Linux infrastructure and complex setup.
recentUpdates: Version 1.1 was released on 2026-11-03, adding build support for real software projects. Version 1.0.2 on 2026-10-31 fixed Claude compatibility, and 1.0.1 on 2026-10-29 added support for Codex, Claude Code, and Pi.
verdict: A valuable, open-source research harness for studying multi-agent scaling and peer coordination, though it is intended for experimental use rather than as a production-ready application.

name: OpenBot
pricingDetail: The desktop application is free for personal, non-commercial use. Commercial use requires a paid license (Starter or Team plans) available via monthly or yearly subscriptions. Optional hosted server services are also available for purchase separately.
description: OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace that enables a team of persistent AI agents to collaborate, share files, and execute workflows on your computer or managed servers. It integrates with various AI models through your existing provider plans, acting as a collaborative layer rather than a standalone model provider.
keyFeatures: Persistent agents with individual workspaces and message histories
Agent-to-agent collaboration and task delegation
Multi-provider support including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and local models
Multi-step automated workflows with approval gates
Local-first architecture keeping data on your machine
bestFor: Users who need persistent AI workflows that span multiple stages, require file access, or benefit from agent teams working together on complex projects.
notIdealFor: Users looking for a simple, single-prompt chatbot experience, or those uncomfortable with agents having broad local system and file access.
recentUpdates: Version 0.78.0 (Nov 24, 2026) introduced voice conversation features in channels and improved server management. Version 0.77.0 (Nov 23, 2026) added OpenBot credits for model-assisted workflows, improved image/video batch generation, and unified terminology for task threads.
verdict: OpenBot is a powerful, highly flexible tool for power users and teams looking to orchestrate AI agents locally, though its development preview status requires users to exercise caution with file and system access.

name: OpenMausBot
pricingDetail: The app is free and open-source (Apache 2.0). Cloud workspace plans for always-on functionality start at $15/month for individuals, with team plans starting at $169/month.
description: MausBot is an open-source, local-first chat interface that organizes AI agents into a messaging-style workspace. It allows users to manage multiple specialist bots, each with its own personality, model, and dedicated cloud computer or local environment.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent management with individual bot profiles and roles
Bring-your-own-model support for Claude, ChatGPT, and others via API keys
Isolated cloud or local VM workspaces with live desktop preview
Approval-based workflow for agent tool use and sensitive actions
Integration with hundreds of apps via Composio including Gmail, Slack, and GitHub
bestFor: Users who already subscribe to AI model providers and want to organize multiple specialized agents within a unified, chat-based interface that supports persistent memory and task delegation.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a fully offline AI experience, as default agents rely on cloud models, or those needing a highly mature enterprise product, given it is currently a 0.1.x version project.
recentUpdates: Version 0.1.181 (2026-11-25) introduced cross-bot skills, GitHub sign-in, unified device management, and optimized Claude endpoint handling. Version 0.1.180 (2026-11-24) introduced Skill Burger, allowing users to view and interact with step-by-step agent task progress in chat.
verdict: A powerful, privacy-focused tool for power users who want deep, granular control over local AI agents and automated workflows without being locked into a single vendor's ecosystem.

name: AutoSwarm
pricingDetail: AutoSwarm is free and open source under the MIT license; users provide their own existing agent CLIs and are responsible for any associated subscription or API costs.
description: AutoSwarm is an open-source orchestration framework that unifies multiple fragmented, independent AI agents into a single coordinated team. It enables these agents to share context, work in parallel, and synthesize results, allowing users to delegate complex tasks to a group of specialized agents through one interface.
keyFeatures: Dynamic agent selection and orchestration
Shared context and organizational memory across agents
Parallel task execution with dependency resolution
Support for major agents including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot CLI
Centralized approval and progress tracking via AutoSwarm Desk
bestFor: Power users who already maintain multiple specialized coding and chat agent CLIs and need to coordinate their efforts on complex, multi-stage projects.
notIdealFor: Users who rely on a single agent, lack existing local agent CLI setups, or require a highly mature, stable product with formal, automated update mechanisms.
recentUpdates: Launched AutoSwarm Desk for Windows and macOS (November 2026); released versions 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 (November 2026) focusing on desktop installation, automatic update mechanisms for the desk app, and bug fixes.
verdict: A powerful, research-backed framework for advanced users that effectively bridges the gap between disparate AI tools, though it is currently an early-stage project that requires significant manual configuration.

name: Lemon Code
pricingDetail: Free (Free usage on Mac and browser, with optional support to bring your own Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini CLI subscription/API key)
description: Lemon Code is an autonomous AI coding agent workspace available for the browser and Mac that writes, runs, and tests code while providing full transparency into terminal outputs and file changes. It automates development workflows by connecting to over 1,500 apps including GitHub, Slack, Linear, and Notion, or custom MCP servers to handle tasks like PR reviews and issue triaging.
keyFeatures: Autonomous agent workspace with terminal, test, and file diff inspection
Integration with 1,500+ third-party apps and custom MCP servers
Scheduled automation for PR reviews, issue-to-PR conversion, and standup reporting
Runs natively in the browser or as a dedicated macOS application
BYO (Bring Your Own) support for Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini CLI
bestFor: Developers and teams seeking to automate repetitive coding chores and cross-app workflows using a browser-accessible or local agent workspace.
notIdealFor: Large organizations requiring enterprise-grade governance features like SSO, SCIM, detailed audit logs, or spend management controls, and developers looking for deep IDE integration for inline code completion.
recentUpdates: On November 22, 2026, the team announced new workflows for planning dependency migrations using the agent.
verdict: Lemon Code provides a highly accessible, free entry point for autonomous agent workflows with excellent visibility into agent actions, though it is a newer tool currently lacking the advanced enterprise management features found in more mature platforms.

name: dsh-superagent
pricingDetail: dsh-superagent is free and open-source under the MIT license. It runs on your own machine inside DeepSeek Harness, so the only costs are the model provider you configure for DSH and any GitHub or Feishu accounts you connect.
description: dsh-superagent is an open-source research prototype designed as a proactive coding agent bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It automates GitHub issue and pull request workflows by operating in isolated sessions to minimize human attention requirements.
keyFeatures: Proactive GitHub repository management and Feishu integration
Isolated agent sessions for individual work items
Agent-guided setup process
Configurable evaluation gates and allow-lists
Dedicated web panel for task monitoring and management
bestFor: Engineering teams and researchers looking to study or adapt proactive, low-attention agent designs within the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem.
notIdealFor: Production environments, teams requiring official support or managed services, or organizations needing multi-repository support.
recentUpdates: The prototype was released on 2026-10-31 along with the design article Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System.
verdict: A rare look at how a frontier lab runs an autonomous, attention-saving coding agent internally, worth studying and trying with DeepSeek Harness, but explicitly a prototype rather than something to depend on.

name: Sandcastle
pricingDetail: Free open source (MIT license)
description: Sandcastle is a TypeScript library and CLI designed to orchestrate AI coding agents within isolated sandbox environments. It automates agent execution, branch management, and the merging of agent-generated commits back into the host repository.
keyFeatures: Native sandboxing with Bubblewrap and Seatbelt
Support for Docker, Podman, E2B, Modal, Vercel, and Fly.io Sprites
Branch strategy management with support for temp branches and merge-back
Built-in agent providers for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, and OpenCode
Programmable orchestration for parallel agents and review pipelines
bestFor: TypeScript developers who need to run multiple parallel, unattended AI coding agents in isolated environments with secure git-based integration.
notIdealFor: Developers requiring a GUI-based agent manager, a fully hosted service, or an API that maintains long-term stability without breaking changes.
recentUpdates: Version 0.14.0 (released 2026-11-02) added isolated sandbox providers for E2B, Modal, and Fly.io Sprites. Version 0.13.0 (released 2026-11-02) established native Bubblewrap and Seatbelt sandboxes as the documented default and improved session resume capabilities.
verdict: A robust, provider-agnostic building block for developers scaling AI agent workflows, though its pre-1.0 status requires careful management of API updates.

name: Agent Autoloop
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (MIT license). Model usage is billed directly to your own provider account.
description: Agent Autoloop is a local, open-source background hub that manages command-line coding agents. It transforms interactive CLI tools into automated background loops, using events like webhooks or cron rules to trigger agents and only alerting you when human input is required.
keyFeatures: Zero-dependency, event-sourced SQLite kernel
Zero-cost wait with session resumption
Plugin support for events, agents, notification channels, and CI/CD delivery
Hop circuit breaker for task recursion control
Automatic management of agent state, logs, and event dispatching
bestFor: Developers using macOS, Linux, or Windows who want to automate existing CLI agents like Claude Code or Codex for scheduled tasks or event-driven workflows with human-in-the-loop approvals.
notIdealFor: Users who require a centralized web dashboard, those uncomfortable with CLI-first configuration, or users who prioritize English-native interfaces, as much of the project's documentation and output defaults to Chinese.
recentUpdates: Recent releases (v1.10.0 through v1.10.2) in late November 2026 introduced performance improvements for Windows path handling, better process management for worker timeouts, and enhanced delivery plugin reporting.
verdict: A powerful and thoughtfully engineered automation tool for power users, though it requires careful rule management and carries a steep learning curve due to its language barrier and CLI-centric design.

name: Capy
pricingDetail: Every plan includes unlimited members, and the plan sets your monthly credits and cloud machine limits. Lite costs $20/mo ($16/mo billed annually) with $20 of credits, and your first 7 days cost $1 with a verified card. Pro costs $100/mo ($80/mo annually) with $105 of credits and adds mobile builds and devices. Max runs from $200 to $1,000/mo in $100 steps with 10% bonus credits. Enterprise is custom and adds SSO/SAML and audit logging. You can bring your own API keys, or a ChatGPT (Codex), GitHub Copilot or SuperGrok subscription, on every plan.
description: Capy is an agent swarm platform for engineering teams that orchestrates thousands of autonomous agents across cloud and local infrastructure to handle complex software tasks. It allows developers to offload maintenance, migrations, and bug fixes to long-lived Captain agents that can operate independently or across distributed environments.
keyFeatures: Captains for multi-agent orchestration
Multiplayer collaboration via Slack and web
Cross-environment execution on cloud VMs or local machines
Automated bug triage, migrations, and code reviews
Live application previews and automated QA testing
bestFor: Engineering teams needing to automate long-horizon tasks like large-scale code migrations, daily bug triage, mobile QA, and incident resolution.
notIdealFor: Developers seeking a purely local-only agent without needing cloud-based orchestration or those requiring non-Linux environments for cloud-based tasks.
recentUpdates: Version 0.10.0 introduced an Issues board for tracking work status, Drive file editing within thread side panes, and significant performance optimizations for the desktop app and cloud machines. Mobile QA support on cloud phones and compatibility with various LLMs, including specialized Daybreak and Flash models, were also added.
verdict: A capable platform for running many cloud agents in parallel, with strong team integrations, model flexibility and unlimited members. Usage is billed in credits, so costs grow with agent activity.

name: Boxes.dev
pricingDetail: Trial is free with 20 box-hours per user. Starter costs $19 per seat per month (50 box-hours), Pro $99 per seat per month (300 box-hours) and Max $249 per seat per month (750 box-hours); extra usage is $0.40 per box-hour from prepaid credits. Enterprise is custom. Standard boxes are 4 vCPU and 8 GB RAM, billed by the second, and model usage runs on your own Codex or Claude subscription or API key.
description: Boxes.dev provides autonomous cloud computers for running Claude Code and Codex agents, ensuring each agent operates within its own isolated Linux environment. By moving development environments to the cloud, it allows developers to manage agent-driven tasks across desktop, mobile, and terminal interfaces without resource constraints.
keyFeatures: Isolated cloud devboxes for parallel agent execution
Multi-agent coordination and messaging
Integration with Slack, Linear, and custom APIs
Early access for building and testing mobile apps
Support for existing Claude Code and Codex subscriptions
bestFor: Developers and teams requiring high-parallelism coding agent workflows where each agent needs a distinct, persistent cloud environment.
notIdealFor: Developers who strictly require local hardware execution, offline operation, or those looking for a platform that includes its own built-in LLM and agent harness.
recentUpdates: Introduced agent-to-agent messaging, early access for iOS/Android testing, improved onboarding UI, and integration support for MCP tools and services like AWS and GitHub as of October 2026.
verdict: A focused, well-designed way to run off-the-shelf coding agents in parallel on real cloud machines, with clear box-hour pricing.

name: Hoplite
pricingDetail: Free plan at $0 with 5 concurrent cloud sessions, sandboxes up to 2 vCPU and 8 GiB, and 5 projects. Team costs $60 per seat per month or $50 per seat per month billed yearly. Enterprise is a custom annual agreement.
description: Hoplite is a cloud-based platform for autonomous coding agents that operate within isolated development environments to handle complex software tasks. It allows teams to manage, share, and automate engineering workflows, including GitHub pull requests and CI triage, through parallelized multi-agent execution.
keyFeatures: Isolated cloud sandboxes with persistent development environments
Multiplayer threads allowing team collaboration and hand-offs
Automated CI triage, pull request generation, and review thread handling
Parallel swarm execution for large-scale migrations
Support for custom scheduling and event-based triggers for automations
bestFor: Engineering teams needing to automate GitHub maintenance, CI triage, and large-scale code migrations using parallelized agents.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring non-GitHub repository hosting or those who prefer keeping all agent activity strictly local to their own machines.
recentUpdates: In November 2026, Hoplite introduced base branch filtering for PR automations, instant local image caching for attachments, and improved subagent visibility within swarms. They also added support for Google's Gemini 4 models and generally available macOS sandboxes for building and testing Apple apps.
verdict: A capable cloud agent product with strong verification and review tooling, best suited to GitHub teams that value product-level QA over raw code output.

name: Replicas
pricingDetail: Free trial with $100 of usage and no card required. Developer costs $50 per month including $50 of usage; Team costs $200 per month and up, in $100 steps, with usage equal to the price; Enterprise is custom. Workspaces bill per minute by size, from $0.004 per minute for 2 vCPU and 8 GB included, and model usage runs on your own subscriptions or API keys.
description: Replicas is a cloud-based platform for engineering teams that runs various coding agents, such as Claude Code and Cursor, in isolated, persistent Linux virtual machines. It integrates directly into existing workflows like Slack, Linear, and GitHub, allowing agents to handle tasks autonomously and return pull requests or completed work.
keyFeatures: Harness-agnostic platform supporting Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, and others
Isolated Linux VM workspaces with warm hooks for pre-configured dependencies
Automated workflows triggered by Slack, Linear, GitHub, GitLab, or webhooks
Visibility and analytics for agent activity, PR velocity, and resource usage
Full computer use capabilities including browser and desktop interaction for verifying work
bestFor: Engineering teams that want to offload recurring maintenance, bug fixes, and feature implementation to autonomous agents running in parallel in the cloud.
notIdealFor: Teams that lack a formal development workflow or those requiring local-only environment execution that cannot be replicated in a cloud-based Linux VM.
recentUpdates: Recent updates include the launch of a new mobile app (November 2026), enhanced autonomous self-fixing codebase capabilities, and the introduction of GPU sandboxes for agent tasks.
verdict: A flexible, harness-agnostic background agent platform with clear usage pricing and strong environment controls.

name: Tembo
pricingDetail: 7-day free trial of Max. Pro costs $60 per month with $90 of monthly usage for up to 5 users; Max costs $200 per month with $400 of monthly usage for up to 10 users; Enterprise is custom. The allowance covers Tembo Gateway model usage and cloud VM compute; your own keys or Claude, Codex or SuperGrok subscriptions add no inference cost.
description: Tembo is an engineering platform that enables teams to delegate coding tasks to autonomous agents running in isolated cloud environments. It integrates with existing tools like GitHub, Linear, and Slack to manage the full lifecycle of a task from trigger and execution to human review and approval.
keyFeatures: Managed cloud-based agent execution environments
Multi-repo operations and automation
Real-time session monitoring and audit logs
Native integrations with Slack, Linear, GitHub, and Sentry
Model-agnostic support for various coding agents and frontier LLMs
bestFor: Engineering teams looking to delegate repeatable, verifiable work—such as dependency upgrades, bug fixes, and documentation updates—to autonomous agents while maintaining human oversight.
notIdealFor: Solo developers who already have reliable local hardware and workflows and do not require a team-oriented platform for shared agent management, analytics, or recurring automations.
recentUpdates: On November 20, 2026, Tembo introduced team-based workspace organization, granular session sharing, and comprehensive audit logs. Previous updates include automatic sandbox scaling based on resource allocation and support for multi-account LLM configurations.
verdict: A broad, well-integrated platform for running any coding agent in complete cloud environments, strongest for teams that need previews and many integrations.

name: Vorflux
pricingDetail: Pay-as-you-go from prepaid credits with no per-seat price: bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Google keys, buy Vorflux tokens at standard provider rates with no platform fee (launch offer), or use a Codex subscription for GPT models. Server compute is billed hourly by size, from Small ($0.2117 per hour, 2 vCPU and 8 GiB) through Medium ($0.4234 per hour), Large ($0.8468 per hour, the default) and Ultra ($1.6934 per hour) to Hyper ($3.3868 per hour, 32 vCPU and 128 GiB), and servers stop after 1 hour idle.
description: Vorflux is a cloud-based AI coding platform that deploys autonomous agents known as AutoBots to handle software development tasks like debugging, testing, and cloud cost management. It integrates into Slack and Git environments to provide 24/7 collaborative coding, PR generation, and infrastructure monitoring.
keyFeatures: Autonomous AutoBots for standing roles like on-call triage and cost management
Isolated cloud execution environments with full repo access
Multi-model support including Claude, GPT, Gemini, and open-source models
Plan Mode for collaborative strategy before code generation
End-to-end testing with video evidence and automated PR reviews
bestFor: Engineering teams needing 24/7 automated support for recurring tasks, CI/CD maintenance, and incident triage.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring strictly local execution without cloud-based environment provisioning or teams with extremely tight data-residency constraints that preclude cloud-based analysis.
recentUpdates: Launched Vorflux 2.0 featuring AutoBots for Slack-integrated, 24/7 autonomous roles and added support for models including GPT-6.1 Terra, Kimi K3.1 Pro, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
verdict: An ambitious team-focused coding agent with strong verification and multi-model review, priced by usage with no token markup.

name: Open Session
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the MIT license. You self-host the server and pay only for your own hardware, sandbox providers and model subscriptions or API keys.
description: Open Session is an open-source, self-hosted agent orchestration platform that provides a control room for coding agents. It allows teams to manage automated coding sessions, pull requests, and agent workflows within isolated Git worktrees on their own infrastructure.
keyFeatures: Self-hosted infrastructure with full control over data and keys
Multiplayer sessions for team collaboration and live agent steering
Isolated Git worktrees and branch management for parallel tasks
Automations triggered by schedules, webhooks, or external channels
Integration with Slack, Linear, Plain, and GitHub
bestFor: Teams that require a self-hosted, forkable agent platform with deep integration into their existing development workflow and full control over security and environment.
notIdealFor: Teams seeking a managed SaaS solution without server maintenance requirements or users who need built-in, hardened authentication without configuring private networks.
recentUpdates: Recent development has been highly active throughout November 2026, including enhancements to the native transcript interface, improved systemd scope handling, and performance optimizations for agent-led workflows.
verdict: A capable open-source alternative to hosted agent platforms for teams willing to run their own server.

name: Nuphos
pricingDetail: Free for up to 3 members and 1 environment with 7 days of audit retention. Dev costs $29 per month, Team $99 per month with unlimited members, Business $299 per month and Scale $999 per month. Model usage runs on your own Claude or ChatGPT account, and cloud computers are billed on a separate team computer plan.
description: Nuphos is an open-source, collaborative workspace designed for DevOps teams to manage and share AI coding agents like Claude Code and Codex. It provides a shared environment for teams to steer agents, integrate with cloud infrastructure, and maintain audit trails with human-in-the-loop approvals.
keyFeatures: Shared sessions for team collaboration and agent steering
Human-in-the-loop approval plans for infrastructure changes
Self-hostable backend and agent runtime under Apache 2.0 license
Cross-platform support with Desktop, CLI, and iOS applications
Integrated support for GitHub, Linear, Kubernetes, Grafana, and cloud providers
bestFor: DevOps and platform teams that already utilize coding agents and require a collaborative, secure, and audited workspace for managing infrastructure tasks.
notIdealFor: Teams looking for fully autonomous agents that operate without human approval, or users expecting an all-in-one AI service that includes model inference subscriptions.
recentUpdates: On 2026-11-08, Nuphos introduced a new paper-and-ink design system for the desktop app. Throughout October 2026, the platform released multiple security updates for self-hosted backends, added session search and personal skills, and transitioned to an open-source model under the Apache 2.0 license.
verdict: A promising open-source team workspace for agent-driven operations work, still evolving quickly in early access.

name: Obeya
pricingDetail: Obeya is free and open-source under the MIT licence and runs locally. Its agents use the official Claude Code or Codex installation on your machine, so your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription and its usage limits apply.
description: Obeya is a spatial workspace for directing AI coding agents as an engineering director would. It organizes tasks as cards on a canvas where agents perform work in the background and provide narrated demos for review and approval.
keyFeatures: Spatial canvas for organizing AI agent tasks and projects
Narrated demo-based review process for agent-completed work
Support for parallel task execution with dependency management
Review cards for analyzing external pull requests before execution
Voice and text interaction with agents in English and German
bestFor: Developers who delegate coding to Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini and prefer managing multiple parallel tasks via demo reviews instead of manual diff analysis.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring manual verification of every line of code written by agents or developers using AI agents outside of the supported Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini platforms.
recentUpdates: Recent updates include expanded agent support to Gemini, background process management improvements, the ability for agents to operate in Chrome, and enhanced pausing/resuming functionality for agent tasks across all card types.
verdict: An early but actively shipped take on agent orchestration built around demo review; worth a look if you run several Claude Code or Codex agents at once.

name: Vespin
pricingDetail: Vespin does not publish pricing on its site. Agents run on your own Claude or ChatGPT plan or your own Anthropic or OpenAI API keys, and Vespin can move an agent to the next plan or key when one hits its usage limit.
description: Vespin is a unified workspace and inbox designed for managing autonomous coding agents like Claude Code and Codex. It centralizes communications by having agents post to a single inbox only when they require human intervention, such as decisions, to-dos, or code reviews.
keyFeatures: Unified inbox for agent requests and task management
Support for running agents in cloud sandboxes or on local machines
Slack and terminal integration for initiating tasks
Ability for agents to hand off work, message each other, and create sub-tasks
Automations triggered by GitHub events, schedules, or webhooks
bestFor: Developers and small teams managing multiple autonomous coding agents who want to centralize their workflows and pull request reviews.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring publicly available pricing tiers, those using agents other than Claude Code or Codex, or users on Windows or Linux desktop environments (though Linux servers are supported as machine runners).
recentUpdates: Version 0.41.1 (2026-11-24) improved MCP server reporting and header UI; version 0.40.0 (2026-11-20) introduced Vespin in Slack and a redesigned settings interface.
verdict: Vespin is an efficient, inbox-first tool for orchestrating coding agents, offering a polished experience for teams that want to delegate tasks to AI while retaining oversight through a clean interface.

name: AgentRun
pricingDetail: AgentRun is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 licence and runs on your laptop, in one container or on your own server. You bring your own model keys (OpenRouter, Anthropic or OpenAI), so model usage is billed by those providers.
description: AgentRun is an open-source platform for running managed agents on top of a coding-agent harness such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or pi. It adds self-improvement, durable execution and a control plane: agents keep notes, skills and learned workflows from each run, runs survive restarts, and one console shows approvals, failures, spend and results.
keyFeatures: Durable execution with crash recovery and state persistence
Self-learning that converts repeated steps into reusable workflows
Agent management console for monitoring cost, status, and timelines
Support for multiple agent harnesses including pi, Claude Code, and Codex
Granular control with spend caps, approval workflows, and human-in-the-loop intervention
bestFor: Teams using TypeScript who have repeated agentic workflows that require visibility, auditability, and cost reduction through the conversion of agent loops into structured, deterministic code paths.
notIdealFor: Simple tasks that can be solved with a single function, or production environments requiring a fully managed durable scheduler, native Python support, or a built-in production support SLA.
recentUpdates: The platform was introduced on November 10, 2026, featuring a focus on token reduction through self-learning workflows. As of late November 2026, the core DSL package remains in beta (version 0.1.0-beta.4).
verdict: A promising open-source control plane for repeat agent work, with a distinctive learning loop; still in beta, so expect fast changes.

name: Lody
pricingDetail: The Lody client, CLI and daemon are open source under the Apache-2.0 licence. The hosted workspace has Free, Plus and Enterprise plans listed on lody.ai/price. Agents run on your own machines with the subscriptions, logins and model keys already configured there, so model usage is billed by those providers.
description: Lody is a collaborative workspace that enables teams to manage multiple coding agents and parallel work sessions across desktop, mobile, and browser environments. It serves as a central control plane for various AI coding tools, allowing teams to share context, review diffs, and automate tasks through a unified interface.
keyFeatures: Parallel agent management with isolated Git worktrees
Support for 40+ agents including Claude Code, Codex, and DeepSeek Harness
Cross-machine collaboration with shared sessions and mobile access
GitHub integration for PR binding, CI sync, and automated review loops
Local-first architecture using CRDTs for synchronized team context
bestFor: Software teams looking to coordinate multiple AI coding agents, maintain shared context across different machines, and automate recurring tasks or PR reviews within a unified workspace.
notIdealFor: Users who require a purely cloud-based execution environment without any local machine or CLI dependency, or those who need deep GitHub-specific automations outside of a Git-based workflow.
recentUpdates: Version 0.114.0 (2026-11-23) introduced EverMe for account-wide memory, a new Today outline for session task management, enhanced status view for organizing sessions, and improved background command execution.
verdict: A polished way to turn individual coding agent sessions into shared team work across desktop and mobile, built on agents you already pay for.

name: LoopForge
pricingDetail: LoopForge is free and open-source under the MIT licence and runs on your own infrastructure with Docker. Model usage is not included: each user brings credentials for the coding-agent CLI they pick, billed by that provider.
description: LoopForge is a self-hosted, open-source AI delivery platform that enables engineering teams to automate software development through standardized, repeatable workflows. It orchestrates various coding agents within isolated Docker sandboxes, incorporating human gates and automated testing to ensure quality and auditability.
keyFeatures: Visual SOP designer for defining agent-based delivery pipelines
On-demand cloud workspaces with isolated Docker sandboxes
Support for multiple coding agent CLIs including Claude Code, CodeBuddy, and Codex
Automated build, test, and human review gates for every task
Integrated token cost accounting and execution history tracking
bestFor: Engineering teams requiring repeatable, reviewable, and transparent software delivery processes with fixed roles, testing, and human sign-off.
notIdealFor: Single developers without audit requirements, untrusted multi-tenant environments, or teams lacking Docker and database infrastructure management capabilities.
recentUpdates: Version 0.4.0 (2026-11-17) introduced scheduled task history, MR/PR nodes in SOPs, and enhanced agent CLI management within workspaces.
verdict: A serious open-source take on agent delivery pipelines with human gates, best suited to teams willing to self-host.

name: Timon
pricingDetail: Timon is free and open-source under the GNU AGPL v3 (with an exception that lets plugins use any licence; the SDK and plugin templates are MIT). The free edition includes agents, missions, Kanban, memory, routines, every bundled module and plugin, and all clients. A Pro licence adds several users, roles and groups, per-person permissions and support; it never replaces your agent CLI subscription, and Timon never calls a token-billed API on your behalf.
description: Timon is a desktop workstation and background service for AI coding agents that consolidates multiple CLIs into a single, orchestrated environment. It manages project tasks through a Kanban board, automating the coding, review, and merge process using git worktrees.
keyFeatures: One workspace for multiple AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot
Automated pipeline with coder, reviewer, and merger roles
Model switching mid-conversation while maintaining full context
Background daemon for continuous autonomous task execution
Multichat interface for side-by-side agent interaction
bestFor: Developers who already pay for multiple coding agent subscriptions and want to automate git-based task backlogs on their own hardware.
notIdealFor: Developers who only use a single agent, require non-git workflows, or need a tool with published pricing before starting.
recentUpdates: Version 0.1.10 (2026-11-24) introduced GitHub pull request integration with conflict resolution, refined GitHub publishing workflows, and disabled the Antigravity backend by default.
verdict: An ambitious, early-stage local workstation that packages a plan, code, review and merge loop around the agent CLIs developers already use.

name: SoduWork
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the MIT license and self-hosted. Solo use runs locally; team deployments add a self-hosted Hub. Model usage is billed by the providers you configure.
description: SoduWork is an AI-native engine that coordinates teams and their agents through a shared workspace. It provides a governance layer for multi-harness agent workflows, ensuring that tasks are defined by acceptance criteria, reviewed by independent AI agents, and signed off by humans.
keyFeatures: Multi-harness support for switching between models like Pi, OpenCode, and DeepSeek
Independent AI-driven review against user-defined acceptance criteria
Versioned team plugins to codify and reuse successful workflows
Self-hosted Hub architecture for audit trails and permission management
Integrated issue pool for tracking requests, agent execution, and human sign-off
bestFor: Engineering teams that require governed, reproducible agent workflows with formal acceptance criteria, review steps, and clear approval records.
notIdealFor: Solo developers looking for a simple, low-overhead coding assistant, as the Hub, runner, and governance components introduce significant setup complexity.
recentUpdates: Released version 1.13.19 on 2026-11-19, following version 1.13.18 on 2026-11-18 which improved conversation settings and automations, and version 1.13.17 on 2026-11-16 which introduced new chat folder handling and updated runtime options.
verdict: One of the more complete open-source team layers for multi-harness agent work, with review and sign-off as first-class steps; still in public beta.

name: TaroBird
pricingDetail: TaroBird is free and open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence, with desktop builds for macOS and Windows, an iOS App Store app and an Android APK. It does not include AI engines, model accounts or credits; Bots run on the CLIs and plans you already have installed.
description: TaroBird is a self-hosted messaging workspace that aggregates command-line coding agents into a unified interface for desktop and mobile devices. It runs official CLI agents locally, allowing users to coordinate multi-bot workflows, remote tasks, and cross-computer collaboration.
keyFeatures: Unified interface for official CLI agents like Claude Code, Codex, and DeepSeek Harness
Cross-device synchronization between desktop and mobile
ADHD mode for managing up to 12 parallel conversations
Agent Bus and multi-bot groups for orchestrated workflows
Chancellor mode for task delegation via tracked tickets
bestFor: Developers who manage multiple agent CLIs across their own machines and require a centralized, remote-accessible interface to dispatch, monitor, and approve AI-driven tasks.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring a hosted, managed SaaS service, users who exclusively need Linux desktop clients, or those who cannot utilize AGPL-3.0 licensed software.
recentUpdates: Version 1.6.0 (released 2026-11-23) introduced support for Pi and Antigravity engines, conversation forking and rewinding, remote phone screen viewing, and enhanced workspace UI elements like quota indicators.
verdict: An ambitious, actively shipped way to turn the agent CLIs on your own hosts into a team you can message from anywhere.

name: OpenComputer
pricingDetail: Self-hosting is free under Apache-2.0: you pay your cloud and model provider. OpenComputer Cloud is billed per Slack workspace for work minutes: a 3-day free trial with 600 work minutes and $10 of model tokens, Pro at $20 per month (2,000 work minutes), Max at $200 per month (25,000 work minutes) and custom Enterprise pricing above 60,000 minutes. Extra minutes cost $0.01 from prepaid credits. Bring your Claude or ChatGPT subscription or an API key, or use OpenComputer's tokens at API prices with no markup.
description: OpenComputer is an open-source, self-hostable cloud coding agent for teams. Mention @Computer in a Slack thread or call the API, and it runs Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode on a warm cloud Linux machine, with each thread in its own isolated session and branch, and returns a pull request the whole thread can watch and steer.
keyFeatures: Persistent cloud Linux VMs with stateful disks
Slack-based agent interaction and steering
Isolated session management using rootless Podman
Self-hostable on AWS, GCP, Azure, or OCI
Native support for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode
bestFor: Teams using Slack that want a shared, persistent cloud coding agent environment that avoids the latency of ephemeral sandboxes.
notIdealFor: Teams that do not use Slack, developers requiring native macOS or Windows build environments, or those seeking shell access to the agent's underlying sessions.
recentUpdates: Launched on Show HN as an open-source alternative to Devin on November 20, 2026; release v0.6.0.50 published on November 9, 2026.
verdict: A fast, fully open-source take on the Slack-driven cloud coding agent that reuses the harnesses your team already trusts.

name: InstaBox
pricingDetail: Free plan with 1 machine (4 vCPU / 8 GiB), a fixed 20 GiB disk and 5 snapshots. Pro costs $20 a month, Builder $100 and Team $500, each including that amount in monthly credits, plus usage billed by the second ($0.004 per vCPU-hour, $0.00225 per GiB-hour of memory, GPUs from $0.49 per hour). Enterprise is custom.
description: InstaBox provides isolated, ephemeral Linux virtual machines designed for autonomous agents and AI-driven development. The platform allows machines to auto-pause when idle, ensuring cost-efficiency by billing only for active runtime.
keyFeatures: Ephemeral microVMs with persistent disk state
Pre-installed agent toolkit including CLI and MCP server
GPU support (NVIDIA T4, A100, H100, L4) for AI workloads
Automated CI runners and GitHub Actions integration
Secure secrets management via outbound proxies
bestFor: Running untrusted AI-generated code, coding agents, automated CI workflows, and remote development environments.
notIdealFor: 24/7 web hosting or long-running services that require constant uptime without any idle periods, as the platform is optimized for bursty, task-based agent workloads.
recentUpdates: Introduced the ability to convert personal accounts to workspaces (2026-11-22), live system status tracking (2026-11-21), warm CI runners from snapshots (2026-11-21), and support for H100 and T4/A100 GPU machines (2026-11-17/18).
verdict: A capable cloud runtime for agents, with forking, GPUs and multi-OS desktops behind a single npx command.

name: Brickie
pricingDetail: Free and open source under the MIT licence. You run it on your own Docker host or Kubernetes cluster and pay for your own compute and object storage; it needs a Hatchet engine, either self-hosted Hatchet Lite or Hatchet Cloud.
description: Brickie is Hatchet's open-source provider for running durable sandboxes for AI agents in your own cloud or Kubernetes cluster. Each sandbox session is a container with a shell and a workspace, every call that changes the workspace saves an immutable, forkable snapshot to object storage, and every sandbox call runs as a retryable, observable Hatchet task.
keyFeatures: Durable, forkable filesystem snapshots
Hatchet-guaranteed safe task retries
Flexible runtime support including Kata, gVisor, and AWS Nitro
FIPS 140-3 compliant workloads with signed images
mTLS for secure communication between provider and sandboxes
bestFor: Teams building agent-based products who need to self-host their sandbox infrastructure for security or compliance requirements.
notIdealFor: Developers looking to run individual coding agents remotely or those seeking a managed, zero-infrastructure sandbox service.
recentUpdates: Brickie was officially released on November 23, 2026. Recent versions (0.1.5 through 0.1.7) released in mid-November 2026 include improvements to sandbox deletion, metadata inheritance for forks, and fixes for file staging replays.
verdict: A solid self-hosted sandbox layer whose durable, snapshot-per-call design suits long-running agents; best value for teams already on Hatchet.

name: Bolt.new
pricingDetail: Free plan available with daily token limits and hosting restrictions. Paid tiers include Pro ($25/month), Teams ($30/month), and custom Enterprise contracts. A Lite plan ($9/month) is also offered for Forge-based usage.
description: Bolt.new is an AI-powered browser-based web development agent that allows users to prompt, build, run, and deploy full-stack applications without local setup. Utilizing StackBlitz's WebContainers technology, it provides a functional development environment with built-in hosting, databases, and authentication.
keyFeatures: Full-stack development environment in the browser
Choice of AI agents for code generation
Integrated database hosting and management
Direct GitHub integration and zip export
Built-in security audits and database security checks
bestFor: Founders, developers, and designers looking to rapidly build and deploy web app prototypes, MVPs, and marketing websites without local environment setup.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring non-JavaScript backends like Python or PHP, or users who require highly predictable, fixed pricing due to token-based consumption.
recentUpdates: As of November 2026, Link by Stripe handles subscription billing. An opt-out setting for AI training on user content was introduced in October 2026, and security audit features were expanded to allow 30 free checks daily on paid plans.
verdict: Bolt.new is an excellent tool for developers and founders who prioritize code ownership and a true development environment over simple chat-based scaffolding, though it falls short for native mobile app production.

name: v0
pricingDetail: Offers a Free plan, Plus ($30/user/month), Business ($100/user/month), and custom Enterprise plans. A Premium plan ($20/month) exists but is being sunsetted for new users.
description: v0 is an AI-powered development platform that generates production-ready, full-stack web applications from natural language prompts. It integrates directly with the Vercel ecosystem, providing a collaborative environment for building, iterating, and deploying React-based applications.
keyFeatures: AI-powered code generation for Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui
Integrated Git workflow with automatic branch creation and pull request management
Built-in VS Code-style editor with real-time previews and error diagnostics
Secure database integrations including Snowflake and AWS
Agentic capabilities for autonomous debugging, web search, and multi-step task execution
bestFor: React and Next.js developers, product managers, and designers within the Vercel ecosystem who need to ship production-ready UIs and full-stack applications quickly.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring non-React stacks, developers needing offline capabilities, or those who prefer hosting providers other than Vercel, as the platform is heavily optimized for that specific infrastructure.
recentUpdates: In 2026, v0 evolved into a full development environment with Git integration, a built-in code editor, and agentic workflows. Recent updates also include support for reading npm credentials from shared environment variables and integration with Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.
verdict: v0 is the premier AI tool for the React and Next.js ecosystem, successfully transitioning from a simple UI generator to a robust, production-ready development platform that fits seamlessly into professional Git-based workflows.

name: Lovable
pricingDetail: Offers a Free plan with daily usage limits and three paid tiers (Pro, Business, Enterprise) based on monthly credit allocations. Pro and Business plans range from 100 to 10,000 credits per month with options for monthly or annual billing.
description: Lovable is an AI development platform that generates full-stack web applications from plain language descriptions. It handles the frontend, backend, database, authentication, and integrations while providing users with full ownership of the generated code.
keyFeatures: AI-powered full-stack application generation
Shared workspaces with role-based access control
Built-in backend and database infrastructure
Git synchronization with GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket
Custom domain support and automated hosting
bestFor: Founders, product managers, and agencies needing to rapidly build SaaS products, internal tools, dashboards, or client portals with full code ownership.
notIdealFor: Users requiring specific frameworks like Next.js, those building native mobile apps for app stores, or organizations needing strictly predictable monthly pricing.
recentUpdates: Recent updates include support for managed Google Maps on custom domains, Databricks publishing, automated test user creation for browser testing, and integration with Asaas for Brazilian payment processing.
verdict: Lovable is a powerful, enterprise-grade AI engineer that bridges the gap between no-code speed and pro-code flexibility, making it an excellent choice for teams needing to ship production applications quickly.

name: Replit
pricingDetail: Core ($18/month billed annually or $20/month) is the entry plan for new sign-ups, and Pro is $90/month billed annually or $100/month, with higher credit limits, more collaborators and advanced features. The free Starter plan is no longer listed on the pricing page, though Replit's docs still describe it with daily Agent credits and one published app. Free Mode is included Agent usage within each plan's allowance, not a separate plan. Custom Enterprise plans are available.
description: Replit is a cloud-based development environment that combines an AI-powered coding agent, hosting, and collaboration tools in a single browser interface. It allows users to build, test, and deploy full-stack applications without needing local environment setup.
keyFeatures: Replit Agent 4 for prompt-to-app development
Design Canvas for visual UI prototyping
Intelligent Model Routing for cost-efficient AI tasks
Built-in full-stack infrastructure including databases and hosting
Collaborative Workspaces for team development
bestFor: Technical founders, students, and small teams looking to rapidly build and ship MVPs, internal tools, or prototypes without local environment configuration.
notIdealFor: Professional developers managing large, existing codebases or users who require strictly predictable monthly billing costs.
recentUpdates: In August 2026, Replit introduced Free Mode for everyday AI work within plan allowances. In September 2026, Replit removed the free Starter plan from its pricing page, making Core the entry point for new users.
verdict: Replit is an excellent all-in-one solution for developers and teams looking to minimize environment setup and maximize productivity through integrated AI, hosting, and collaboration.

name: Playcode
pricingDetail: Free plan available with limited features. Pro plan is $17/month billed annually ($199/year) or $19/month billed monthly. Max plan starts at $100/month. Credits are used for AI building tasks, and paid plans include higher credit allowances, custom domains, and hosting for Cloud apps.
description: Playcode is an AI-powered platform for building and hosting web and mobile applications using conversational language. It allows users to create full-stack apps with databases, authentication, and custom domains, while also providing tools to export code for external hosting.
keyFeatures: AI-driven conversational app building
Real-time browser preview and live debugging
Full-stack cloud hosting with database and backend support
Custom domain support and automated deployments
Project version control with rollback capabilities
bestFor: Non-technical individuals or teams who need to rapidly build and host custom, full-stack business applications like CRMs, booking systems, and client portals.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring high-level industry compliance certifications like SOC 2, ISO, or HIPAA, as well as teams that prefer visual, manual drag-and-drop interface builders.
recentUpdates: In November 2026, Playcode introduced web search capabilities for apps, enabled keyword research for 94 countries, added voice interaction with the AI agent, and integrated advanced models like Gemini 4 Neon and GPT-6.2.
verdict: Playcode is a highly efficient, AI-centric development environment that bridges the gap between no-code builders and traditional coding by allowing users to build complex, exportable applications entirely through chat.

name: Emergent
pricingDetail: Offers a Free tier with limited credits, a Standard plan starting at $17/month (annual) or $20/month (monthly), and a Pro plan starting at $167/month (annual) or $200/month (monthly).
description: Emergent is an AI-powered, agentic development platform that allows users to build, test, and publish full-stack web and mobile applications using natural language. It handles the entire stack including frontend, backend, database, and hosting, enabling rapid prototyping and app delivery without requiring manual coding.
keyFeatures: Natural language app generation
Full-stack development (React, Next.js, Python/FastAPI)
Built-in hosting and database integration
Web to React Native mobile app conversion
Automated testing and iterative chat-based updates
bestFor: Founders and non-developers looking to quickly prototype or build internal tools, MVPs, and dashboards using natural language.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring heavy custom design, high-security financial or medical applications, or users who require fast performance on mobile devices.
recentUpdates: As of October 16, 2026, mobile app hosting now incurs an additional 10-credit fee per month; internal documentation updates throughout late 2026 have clarified credit usage for deployment tiers.
verdict: Emergent is a powerful, high-growth 'vibe-coding' platform that successfully bridges the gap between natural language ideas and production-ready software by automating the entire development lifecycle.

name: Bitrig
pricingDetail: Free plan includes 10 daily messages and 60 monthly credits. Pro plan is $25/month, providing unlimited daily messages and 200 monthly credits.
description: Bitrig is a Mac-based development environment that utilizes AI to build and ship native Swift applications for all Apple platforms. It integrates with real Xcode projects, providing a professional-grade workflow that allows users to export their code and manage app distribution directly to TestFlight and the App Store.
keyFeatures: AI-powered native Swift code generation using Claude and OpenAI models
Full Xcode toolchain support with real Xcode project compatibility
Built-in 3D simulators and live device testing via Bitrig Remote
Figma design-to-Swift conversion using Apple-standard UI components
Automated App Store and TestFlight distribution workflow
bestFor: Developers and beginners who want to build high-fidelity native Apple applications while leveraging AI to manage the complexity of Xcode, system APIs, and App Store publishing.
notIdealFor: Users who do not have access to an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS Tahoe or later, or those seeking a non-Apple-focused development platform.
recentUpdates: On November 18, 2026, Bitrig added the ability to track and resolve GitHub pull requests via AI. Previous updates in late 2026 introduced real device testing in the Preview tab, 3D recording features, and Supabase backend integration.
verdict: Bitrig is a powerful, AI-first development tool that effectively streamlines the native Apple app development lifecycle, from initial idea to App Store publication.

name: Floot
pricingDetail: Free plan includes 100 build actions per day and limited storage. Pro ($25/mo) and Power ($100/mo) plans increase build action limits, storage, and offer features like custom domains, removed badges, code export, and increased native app builds.
description: Floot is a platform that enables users to build, host, and publish full-stack TypeScript and React applications by describing them to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor. It functions as a remote MCP server, providing managed backend services including a Postgres database, authentication, file storage, and hosting without requiring local infrastructure or command-line tools.
keyFeatures: Full-stack integration including managed Postgres, auth, and hosting
Built-in services for email, payments, and shipping with zero-code setup
Real-time app preview directly inside the AI chat interface
Firewall protection with traffic logging and human verification
Native app builds for Google Play and the Apple App Store
bestFor: Developers or founders who already use Claude or ChatGPT and want to build, prototype, or ship full-stack web apps without managing infrastructure or complex deployments.
notIdealFor: Teams that require Git-based workflows, developers who need to host data outside of the United States, or users looking for a traditional visual drag-and-drop builder.
recentUpdates: Recent updates as of November 2026 include the ability for AI assistants to view and test apps via a dedicated browser session without manual user intervention, a new firewall service for managing traffic and bot protection, and enhanced preview capabilities that display live apps directly within the chat interface for Claude.
verdict: Floot is a highly effective platform for leveraging existing AI subscriptions to ship production-ready applications, provided you are comfortable with its managed, U.S.-hosted infrastructure and daily build action limits.

name: Dyad
pricingDetail: Free forever version available. Pro plan costs $20/month including 200 AI credits; Max plan costs $79/month including 900 AI credits.
description: Dyad is an open-source, local-first AI app builder that allows users to create web applications by describing ideas in plain English. It keeps project files on the user's machine and provides flexibility by supporting both local AI models and various cloud-based API providers.
keyFeatures: Local-first project storage and code ownership
Model-agnostic architecture supporting local models and cloud providers
Agentic Build mode for iterative, multi-step development
Integrated Supabase and Neon database connectivity
MCP (Model Context Protocol) support for external tool integration
bestFor: Builders who prioritize owning their source code, working locally, and maintaining control over their AI models and hosting environments.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a fully managed, browser-only experience who do not want to manage API keys, dependencies, or local environment configurations.
recentUpdates: Version 1.25.0-beta.1 introduced improved Neon Auth branch migrations and enhanced Supabase token counting. Version 1.13.0 added an iterative, agentic Build mode for large codebases and a revamped model picker.
verdict: Dyad is a powerful, transparent, and flexible tool for builders who prioritize local control and avoiding vendor lock-in, offering a superior alternative for those who want their code to remain independent of the builder's infrastructure.

name: Onlook
pricingDetail: Onlook is free to use with your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription. The desktop application is free to download and self-host, while custom enterprise pricing is available for teams requiring features like advanced security, SSO, and team-based project management.
description: Onlook is an open-source, local-first desktop application that functions as an agentic design canvas for existing codebases. It allows designers and engineers to interactively edit and prototype real applications by connecting their own AI subscriptions to perform code-level updates through a visual interface.
keyFeatures: Design directly on a live local development server
Bring your own AI agent (Claude or ChatGPT/Codex)
Infinite canvas for side-by-side explorations and state variations
Native Git integration for pull requests and version control
Creation of shareable HTML artifacts
bestFor: Design engineers, product designers, and frontend developers who want to iterate on real React-based products while maintaining a single source of truth in their codebase.
notIdealFor: Teams needing a fully cloud-hosted design platform, users on Linux, or those seeking a tool to generate entire new applications from scratch without an existing codebase.
recentUpdates: On November 19, 2026, the company launched a complete rebuild of its desktop application as an open-source agentic design tool, moving to a local-first architecture and open-sourcing the project under the Apache 2.0 license.
verdict: Onlook is a powerful, category-defining tool for 'Visual Engineers' that successfully eliminates the gap between design mockups and shipped code by making the editor an extension of your existing IDE and repository.

name: Base44
pricingDetail: Offers a Free tier and four paid tiers (Starter $16/mo, Builder $40/mo, Pro $80/mo, Elite $160/mo, billed annually). Pricing is based on a dual-credit system: message credits for AI-assisted development and integration credits for live app operations.
description: Base44 is a no-code AI app builder that allows users to create functional applications, websites, and AI agents by describing them in plain language. The platform provides an integrated backend, database, and authentication system, allowing users to move from an idea to a live, production-ready app without manual setup.
keyFeatures: AI-powered app and website generation using natural language
Integrated backend, database, and authentication system
Real-time visual editor with drag-and-drop customization
GitHub integration for code access and version control
