recentUpdates: On November 10, 2026, the project added the youfang stack with magic-move-deck. On November 6, 2026, it integrated the optional req-tpm stack. On October 29, 2026, the project enabled one-command installation for Claude Code and Codex and renumbered Engineering Notes companions.
verdict: A practical, non-theoretical playbook that successfully converts abstract engineering best practices into actionable, agent-executable skills.

name: CallMeMCP
pricingDetail: The iPhone/Android app is a subscription: $4.99 per week with a 3-day trial for new accounts, or $24.99 per year. The hosted MCP server itself requires no account, API key, or OAuth; the phone number routes calls.
description: CallMeMCP is a specialized bridge between AI agents and users, allowing agents to initiate phone calls or send text notifications to a mobile device. It uses a custom MCP server to facilitate remote interactions, enabling users to hear agent queries via a synthetic voice and provide spoken responses that are transcribed back as text.
keyFeatures: Native phone calls via iOS CallKit and Android call screens
Spoken-to-text transcription for agent-human interaction
Thread-based agent management for tracking sessions
Support for both one-way notifications and two-way conversations
MCP-compliant architecture requiring no API keys or OAuth
bestFor: Solo developers running long, unattended AI agent sessions who need to provide approvals or make decisions while away from their keyboard.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a free service, a general-purpose voice assistant, or highly audited, zero-retention security environments.
recentUpdates: Version 1.6.9 was released in November 2026, adding new subscription tiers, following version 1.6.7 which introduced monthly and yearly billing options.
verdict: A focused, easy-to-set-up way to keep long agent runs moving by reaching you by phone, with sensible privacy defaults. However, it is subscription-only, iOS/Android app dependent, and carries unresolved high-severity scan findings and unverified publisher ownership.

name: Interfaces Skills
pricingDetail: The skills are free and open-source under the MIT license. Running them only costs whatever your AI coding agent subscription or API usage already costs.
description: Interfaces Skills is a collection of agent skills designed to help AI coding agents build, review, and polish user interfaces. It covers domains including accessibility, layout, typography, color systems, and UI polish to ensure interfaces meet high quality standards.
keyFeatures: better-interface: A comprehensive cross-discipline review producing a ranked severity report
interface-review: Automated checks for interface regressions in branches, PRs, or uncommitted changes
Component workflows: Includes break, state-machine, and variant skills for rendering and stress-testing UI components
Build capabilities: Uses build-design to convert Figma files or design images into code using project-specific tokens
Accessibility audits: Checks components and flows against WCAG 2.2 criteria
bestFor: Frontend and design engineers using AI agents who need detailed, opinionated guidance to improve visual and accessibility quality in their generated UI.
notIdealFor: Backend-focused development or teams that require a deterministic, CI-backed linter rather than an agent-driven, prompt-based review process.
recentUpdates: Version 1.17.0 was released on October 25, 2026, featuring enhancements to the teardown viewer, with consistent repository updates throughout November 2026.
verdict: One of the most thorough UI-quality skill packs for coding agents, grounded in its author's published design-engineering writing and easy to drop into existing agent setups.

name: Traycer
pricingDetail: Free for individuals with bring-your-own-agent subscriptions (no token metering); Sync team plan is $20/user/month or $16/user/month billed yearly. Optional pay-as-you-go inference credits ($1 = 1 credit, 20% markup on Traycer-provided models) and cloud sandboxes cost extra.
description: Traycer is an open-source desktop workspace designed for orchestrating AI coding agents by providing a shared environment for tasks, planning, and documentation. It acts as a supervision layer that connects to your existing coding agent subscriptions, allowing agents to work in parallel, communicate with each other, and maintain shared context across worktrees.
keyFeatures: Agent-to-agent communication and orchestration
Bring Your Own Subscription (BYOS) for 22+ supported coding agents
Shared workspace for artifacts, specs, and tickets
Isolated git worktrees for parallel agent execution
Cross-device cloud synchronization
bestFor: Developers who already pay for coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex and want to reduce drift by enforcing a spec-first planning workflow.
notIdealFor: Users who do not currently use a capable coding agent, developers performing only small or trivial tasks where planning latency adds unnecessary friction, or teams with established ticket-tracking processes in tools like Linear or GitHub Issues.
recentUpdates: Released version 1.5.4 on November 13, 2026, featuring improved memory management, stability, and resource usage optimizations.
verdict: Traycer offers a genuinely usable free tier that avoids double-charging for inference and adds strong multi-agent orchestration and spec-first planning. However, it lacks some enterprise controls (SSO, SCIM, SLA) and advanced PR review features found in competitors like Conductor.

name: TokenEconomizer
pricingDetail: Free and open-source (Apache-2.0). Needs no API key of its own; model usage, including the plugin's own model calls, is billed to the agent plan or key you already use.
description: TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that reduces the cost of AI coding agents by learning from past sessions within a repository to eliminate redundant work. It operates by identifying recurring facts, pruning unused tools, and intervening in failure loops without modifying the agent's underlying model.
keyFeatures: Micro-skills learning to retain repository-specific facts across sessions
Automated tool pruning to remove unused tool definitions from context
Failure-loop intervention using a judge model to redirect stuck agent turns
Repository-specific cost reduction through session history analysis
Local-first storage ensuring all learned data remains on the developer's machine
bestFor: Developers and teams who frequently use AI coding agents on the same repositories and wish to reduce token consumption and operational costs.
notIdealFor: Users who frequently work on one-off tasks in new repositories where history has not accumulated, or users running agent versions outside the specific supported ranges.
recentUpdates: In early November 2026, updates were implemented to reduce loop-guard false alarms and improve documentation regarding model-call costs.
verdict: A credible, research-backed way to trim 18-31% off coding-agent costs on familiar repos; install is still clone-based and pinned to specific agent versions, so expect some upkeep.

name: unslop
pricingDetail: Free (the tool itself is free), requires paid access to coding agents like Claude Code or Codex, and optional image generation services like fal or Replicate incur their own usage fees
description: unslop is a skill for coding agents like Claude Code that transforms vibecoded, AI-generated UI into polished, designed interfaces. It audits screens for common AI aesthetic markers and systematically redesigns them through nine specific passes, covering spacing, color, layout, and visual elements.
keyFeatures: AI-slop audit that identifies design issues like uneven spacing and gradients
Nine-pass redesign process including spacing, color, copy, and layout
Before-and-after story video generation for documentation or sharing
Option to generate professional hero images via integrated services
Live site snapshots to allow redesigning pages without original source code
bestFor: Polishing or redesigning vibecoded dashboards, landing pages, or app screens to remove AI-generated aesthetic markers while retaining original functionality.
notIdealFor: Strict adherence to existing company design systems or building new screens from scratch; it is also not intended for editing prose content.
recentUpdates: Added a plugin installation method for Claude Code on November 15, 2026, and expanded Codex support on November 1, 2026.
verdict: A highly effective and specialized tool for developers looking to elevate the visual craft of AI-generated UI, provided they are comfortable with the inherent design bias of the author's aesthetic.

name: TimeUno
pricingDetail: No free tier; every plan starts with a 14-day free trial requiring a card. Individual is $9.99/month ($8.33/month billed yearly at $99.90), Team is $12.99/seat/month ($10.83/seat/month billed yearly at $129.90) with a 2-seat minimum and free owners/admins, and Enterprise is a custom annual invoiced contract for 25+ seats.
description: TimeUno is an automatic time tracker that monitors work activity in the background without the need for manual timers. It records app and website usage, distinguishes between productive and unproductive time, and provides detailed insights into both human and AI-driven workflows.
keyFeatures: Automatic activity recording with no manual timers required
Deep integration with AI coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor
Categorization of work as productive or unproductive with custom rule-based overrides
Headless Linux agent for tracking AI agents on remote servers
MCP server support for querying time data via AI assistants
bestFor: Freelancers, developers, and small teams who want accurate, automated timesheets and insights into AI-assisted development without intrusive employee monitoring like screenshots.
notIdealFor: Users needing integrated payroll, accounting software connectivity, mobile tracking, or support for shift scheduling and field work.
recentUpdates: As of November 2026, the tool has added support for tracking additional AI tools including Aider, Windsurf, and Ollama, and continues to expand its remote Linux agent capabilities.
verdict: TimeUno's standout feature is treating AI agent time as a first-class, separately tracked metric alongside human hours, with privacy-conscious design (no screenshots stored, prompts and AI answers never sent). The tradeoffs are a paid-only model with card-required trial and default-on screen text reading that may concern privacy-focused users.

name: Executor
pricingDetail: The CLI, desktop app and self-hosted server are MIT-licensed and free. Executor Cloud is free for up to 3 members with unlimited integrations; Team costs $15 per member per month after a 14-day free trial and adds verified domains; Enterprise is custom and adds self-hosted or dedicated cloud deployment support, SSO/SAML, SCIM, audit logs for every tool call and dedicated support.
description: Executor is an open-source MCP gateway that connects AI agents to your services, credentials, and custom automations through a single, unified interface. It allows agents to perform tasks securely by executing code-based tools while keeping credentials hidden from the model.
keyFeatures: Unified MCP endpoint for all agents
Secure credential management with per-tool access policies
Agent-driven TypeScript automation and background task scheduling
Built-in state storage and UI for custom agent-built apps
Self-hosted, cloud-hosted, and local desktop deployment options
bestFor: Developers who use multiple coding agents and require a centralized, governed, and programmable way to manage integrations and credentials.
notIdealFor: Non-technical users who require a visual, drag-and-drop flow builder rather than automation written as code.
recentUpdates: Executor v2 launched in November 2026, introducing a focus on TypeScript apps, code-mode tools, and agent-built automations, with ongoing v2.0.0-beta releases.
verdict: A well-designed, actively developed gateway that removes repeated integration and credential setup across agents, with a free open-source local option and simple per-member cloud pricing.

name: Astryx
pricingDetail: Astryx is free and open-source under the MIT license, including the core components, themes, CLI and the hosted MCP server. There are no paid tiers.
description: Astryx is an open-source design system built on React 19 and StyleX, designed to provide cohesive UI components for both human developers and AI assistants. It offers over 150 accessible components, deep theming capabilities, and a CLI-driven workflow to facilitate rapid development and consistent maintenance.
keyFeatures: 150+ accessible, typed React components
CLI-first architecture for scaffolding, upgrades, and AI context injection
Deep customization via theme-based CSS variables or source ejection
Built-in support for both human and AI-agent workflows
Framework-agnostic styling compatibility via StyleX
bestFor: Teams building React 19+ applications who want a standardized, accessible, and AI-friendly component library that remains highly customizable.
notIdealFor: Projects relying on older versions of React (pre-19) or teams requiring a non-React frontend solution.
recentUpdates: Version 0.7.6 was released on November 2, 2026, and the project became available as a skill in v0 on November 14, 2026. Version 0.7.0 previously introduced improvements to mobile layouts, forms, and CLI integrations.
verdict: A mature, production-tested design system that treats coding agents as first-class users through its CLI and MCP server, making it a strong base for agent-built React UI.

name: devvm
pricingDetail: devvm is free and open-source under the MIT license with no paid tiers. It runs VMs locally on Lima, so the only cost is your own machine; coding agents inside the VM use your existing Claude, ChatGPT or provider subscriptions.
description: devvm is an open-source tool that provides an isolated virtual machine for each individual project folder to safely run coding agents and project toolchains. It leverages Lima to create sandbox environments that limit the blast radius of potential attacks while providing developer-friendly features like port forwarding and secret proxying.
keyFeatures: Per-project isolated virtual machines using Lima
Automated toolchain detection and environment setup
Secure handling of secrets with host-side proxying
Configurable network tiers including restricted allowlists
Support for autonomous coding agents like Claude Code and Codex
bestFor: Developers on macOS or Linux needing a secure, per-project sandbox to run coding agents or manage toolchains without exposing the host system.
notIdealFor: Windows users, Intel Mac users, or teams requiring cloud-hosted sandboxes and enterprise-grade support agreements.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.0-rc.1 was released to improve security hardening by isolating VM proxy secrets and addressing reported bugs; version 0.1.0 was the initial public release on 2026-11-06.
verdict: A focused, security-minded way to sandbox local coding agents per project; very new and still at release-candidate stage.

name: Atuin
pricingDetail: Atuin is free and open-source under the MIT licence. History and thread sync runs on the Atuin Cloud server or a server you host yourself, and sync can be left off entirely. Atuin AI needs an Atuin Hub account (or a self-hosted backend), and its docs say usage is currently free.
description: Atuin replaces standard shell history with an end-to-end encrypted SQLite database that tracks metadata like exit codes, duration, and directory for every command. It also features Atuin Threads, which captures and syncs AI agent sessions, allowing users to search and resume workflows across different machines and agent harnesses.
keyFeatures: End-to-end encrypted shell history sync
Atuin Threads for cross-machine AI agent session resumption
Built-in MCP server for AI agent context access
Context-aware search by directory, host, or session
Atuin AI for natural language command generation
bestFor: Developers who work across multiple machines and use coding agents like Claude Code or Codex, and SREs or DevOps engineers needing deep terminal history insights.
notIdealFor: Occasional terminal users or those who do not use AI coding agents, as the setup and key management requirements may introduce unnecessary friction.
recentUpdates: Version 18.25.1 was released on 2026-11-20. Recent features include Atuin Threads for agent session portability, a 32x speed improvement for sync using packfiles, and an open-sourced AI backend.
verdict: A mature, widely used shell history tool that has grown a practical cross-agent session archive; useful if you already live in the terminal.

name: Modern Web Guidance
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 licence. The CLI runs locally and search works offline; your coding agent's own model and token costs still apply.
description: Modern Web Guidance is a collection of agent skills and an offline CLI that injects expert-vetted web platform best practices and browser compatibility data directly into AI coding agents. It helps agents prioritize modern, performant, and accessible web standards over legacy patterns while assisting in the modernization of existing codebases.
keyFeatures: Expert-vetted library of 200+ web platform guides
Legacy codebase modernization scanner (legacy-scan)
Baseline browser compatibility and fallback data integration
Compatibility with major AI coding agents (Claude Code, etc.)
Public evaluation dashboard for transparency and benchmarking
bestFor: Web developers using AI coding agents who want to ensure their generated code follows modern standards, maintains accessibility, and avoids outdated patterns.
notIdealFor: Backend development, infrastructure management, CI/CD pipelines, or tasks involving non-web-specific tooling like Docker or language-specific configuration files.
recentUpdates: Stable version 1.0 released on 2026-11-10, introducing the modernization workflow, expanded guide database, and cross-browser collaboration with Firefox and Edge. Version 1.0.2 was released on 2026-11-23.
verdict: A well-scoped, cross-browser backed skill that fixes a common weakness of coding agents on frontend work; worth installing for web projects.

name: klad
pricingDetail: klad is source-available, not open source. Building and using it is free for personal use and inside companies with less than 500,000 euros in revenue in their last tax year; larger companies need a bought licence per user. The drawing file format is documented under the MIT licence. Pre-built signed releases are planned and not yet available.
description: Klad is a source-available 2D painting and animation application designed for collaboration between artists and coding agents. It treats every stroke as editable data, allowing users to modify, move, or recolor individual elements generated by agents or drawn by hand.
keyFeatures: Full command-line interface for agent-driven drawing and batch processing
Non-destructive editing of strokes, layers, and animation frames
Direct export to Godot engine for sprites, rigs, and scenes
Timeline with onion skinning, bone rigging, and IK limbs
Pixel art tools with real-time palette-bound color management
bestFor: Indie game artists and illustrators who work alongside coding agents like Claude or Codex to iterate on art stroke-by-stroke.
notIdealFor: Large teams requiring open-source licenses or users who primarily work on Windows and require mature, polished software support for drawing tablets.
recentUpdates: Version 0.4.0 (2026-11-19) introduced an audit of the editor, a new Export menu by format, right-click menu, color sliders, zoom keys, and klad apply --steps for watching script-generated drawings appear mark by mark.
verdict: An inventive, early tool that gives coding agents real brushes rather than an image model; promising for agent-assisted game art.

name: Elephant-Goldfish Model
pricingDetail: Elephant-Goldfish Model is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 licence. It runs inside your coding agent, so that agent's own subscription or API usage applies. Google notes it is not an officially supported Google product.
description: The Elephant-Goldfish Model is an open-source framework and plugin designed to improve AI-assisted software development through a structured, spec-first approach. It separates project context into an 'Elephant' session for drafting specifications and 'Goldfish' sessions for independent, fresh-context adversarial reviews to catch unstated assumptions and blind spots.
keyFeatures: Adversarial AI review using fresh-context subagents
Multi-stage validation workflow (comprehension, criticism, and readiness)
Drift reporting to identify discrepancies between documentation and source code
Customizable review standards and personas
Skill-based orchestration for brainstorming, drafting, and bootstrap documentation
bestFor: Consequential, uncertain, or high-risk software development tasks where thorough design validation is required before implementation.
notIdealFor: Small, well-understood changes, routine bug fixes, or scenarios where token cost and development time overhead outweigh the benefits of rigorous specification review.
recentUpdates: Released version 0.1.1 on November 6, 2026, which added the inventive_catalyst reviewer persona using TRIZ methodology.
verdict: A well-designed, widely adopted workflow for spec-first agent development, with a clever fresh-context review step.

name: opencodex
pricingDetail: opencodex is free and open-source under the MIT licence and runs locally or on your own server. You pay the model providers you connect, or use subscriptions and accounts you already have.
description: opencodex is a lightweight local gateway that acts as a universal provider proxy for AI coding tools like Codex, Claude Code, and Claude Desktop. It translates requests from these tools into the specific API formats required by various LLM providers, allowing users to swap models without modifying the original coding tools.
keyFeatures: Supports 40+ LLM providers including Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, and Ollama
Protocol translation for Responses, Chat Completions, and Anthropic Messages APIs
ChatGPT account pooling with quota-aware routing and thread affinity
Web search and vision sidecars for non-OpenAI models
Cross-platform support for macOS, Windows, and Linux
bestFor: Developers who want to use a variety of LLMs within their preferred coding tools while managing all model API keys and configurations locally.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer a plug-and-play experience without configuring API keys or model endpoints.
recentUpdates: Version v2.100.8 (2026-11-21) introduced Grok Imagine 2.0/Video 1.5 support, added quota/reset parity, enabled live quota updates, and included various bug fixes for context-overflow, reasoning-effort diagnostic analysis, and task state recognition.
verdict: A popular, fast-moving way to point Codex and Claude Code at any model; a good fit if you juggle several providers.

name: Traces
pricingDetail: The Core plan is free for individuals and small teams, with unlimited traces, unlimited teams and up to 50 seats. Larger organizations are asked to get in touch. New organization creation is paused while Traces joins Vercel.
description: Traces is a developer productivity tool that captures, normalizes, and stores AI coding agent sessions into a shared, searchable format for team collaboration. It allows developers to revisit session history, resume work across different agents, and link coding sessions directly to Git commits.
keyFeatures: Unified cross-agent session history for 16+ ecosystems
Git integration to link commits with session context
Interactive Surfaces for visualizing token usage, security, and file changes
Traces MCP server for agent-based lookups and search
Granular privacy controls including PII redaction and visibility settings
bestFor: Engineering teams utilizing multiple coding agents who need a centralized, searchable record of agent workflows tied to their development history.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring fully self-hosted storage solutions or those looking to create new organizational accounts immediately, as new org creation is currently paused.
recentUpdates: On November 16, 2026, Traces announced it is joining Vercel. Earlier in 2026, the platform introduced incremental sharing to improve performance by 15x, support for OpenCode 2.x, and customizable Surfaces for visualizing session data.
verdict: A useful cross-agent layer for keeping and sharing session history, though its future roadmap now sits with Vercel.

name: AgentMon Live
pricingDetail: Free and open-source under Apache-2.0. Runs locally; no account is required and session data stays on your machine.
description: AgentMon Live is Codenotary's open-source monitor for AI coding sessions. It shows live tool calls, subagents, file changes, cost and usage limits in a pane beside Claude Code or in a local browser view, adds a done gate that checks Claude's work before it claims completion, and also lists Codex and Kiro Crew sessions.
keyFeatures: Live dashboard for Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and AWS Kiro sessions
Done gate that validates tests, linting, and build status before completion
Agent flow visualization showing subagent handoffs and tool calls
Cost, context, and quota monitoring with session benchmarking
Privacy-focused local operation with automatic secret masking
bestFor: Developers who want visibility into their AI coding agent workflows, including subagent orchestration, token usage, and automated quality verification.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring collaborative or shared monitoring, as the tool is designed for individual local use and does not support remote team access to the dashboard.
recentUpdates: Version 0.59.0 added feedback buttons and repository starring options. Version 0.57.1 introduced custom web view components like tables and gauges, while recent updates expanded support to OpenAI Codex and AWS Kiro.
verdict: A useful, privacy-preserving visibility layer for multi-session agent work, with the done gate as its most distinctive feature for Claude Code users.

name: agentmash
pricingDetail: The client, hooks and MCP server are open source under MIT. The hosted service has a Free plan with 40 agent-hours a month, one private repo and 7 days of history; Team costs $20 per developer per month ($16 billed annually) with unlimited agent-hours and repos; Enterprise self-hosting starts at $15,000 a year.
description: Agentmash is a coordination layer for AI coding agents that prevents team members from overwriting each other's work. By reporting edits and file claims to a shared room, it provides real-time warnings to agents before they commit changes to conflicting files.
keyFeatures: Real-time collision warnings for AI agents
Agent file claims with automated expiration
Live dashboard for team activity monitoring
Cross-agent coordination across various tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot
Supports local execution via npx and a dedicated desktop lobby app
bestFor: Development teams of two or more developers who use multiple AI agents on a shared repository and frequently encounter merge conflicts.
notIdealFor: Solo developers who do not collaborate with others on a shared repository.
recentUpdates: On October 25, 2026, a new onboarding tour by Mash was introduced. Earlier in October, updates included persistent sidebar history, teammate agent prompting, and room-wide team chat.
verdict: A focused, transparent fix for agents on the same team stepping on each other's edits.

name: bough
pricingDetail: Free and open source under the MIT licence. It runs locally and prices your past work at published API rates; it does not bill you or connect to any service.
description: bough is a local-first utility that visualizes your coding agent session history by parsing logs from Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, and Pi. It breaks down development sessions into individual tasks and prompts, attributing estimated costs based on published API rates to help developers understand project expenditures.
keyFeatures: Automatic discovery of Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Pi session logs
Visual breakdown of work into days, tasks, and prompts with cost attribution
Local-only processing with no telemetry, cloud storage, or external service billing
Filter rail for searching prompts, finding files, and setting spend thresholds
Terminal-based export options including --text and --json outputs
bestFor: Developers using coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, or Pi who want to retrospectively analyze the cost, structure, and difficulty of specific features or past work sessions.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring a shared, live financial dashboard, users seeking actual billed subscription totals, or those needing strictly validated metrics for Pi and Codex workflows.
recentUpdates: Version 0.8.0 released on October 2, 2026, introduced a home page for multi-project management and custom project naming; v0.7.1 and v0.7.0 arrived in late September 2026, adding support for Pi and commit-level cost analysis.
verdict: A thoughtful, fully offline way to turn opaque agent session logs into a readable, priced history of the work.

name: gitfold
pricingDetail: Free and open source, dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0 at your choice. It runs locally on your existing clone and needs no server or account.
description: gitfold is a FUSE-based filesystem for Linux that allows users to mount any Git revision or branch as a directory without needing a full checkout. It enables copy-on-write workspaces that are ideal for coding agents, providing near-instantaneous access to branches while minimizing disk usage.
keyFeatures: Mount any Git revision or branch as a folder
Copy-on-write workspaces that only store changed files
Native Git command support via linked worktrees
Support for branch parent tracking and automatic rebase
Integrated conflict detection and inbox notifications
bestFor: Developers or coding agents working on large monorepos who need to maintain many isolated branches simultaneously without the overhead of full checkouts.
notIdealFor: Build-heavy workflows, small repositories, environments requiring Git LFS, submodules, or platforms other than Linux (such as macOS or Windows).
recentUpdates: Initial public release and announcement made on November 22, 2026.
verdict: A clever, well-documented answer to worktree sprawl for parallel agents on big repos, with honest notes on its FUSE trade-offs.

name: Visual Studio Code
pricingDetail: The editor itself is free for private or commercial use. AI features are available via the GitHub Copilot Free plan (which includes a monthly allowance) or paid Copilot subscriptions; users may also utilize their own API keys or local models without a subscription.
description: Visual Studio Code is a streamlined code editor that supports debugging, task running, and version control alongside optional AI-powered assistance. It provides a highly extensible environment for developers to write, build, and debug applications across a wide range of programming languages.
keyFeatures: Integrated terminal and debugger
AI-powered code suggestions and chat
Multi-agent orchestration in Agents window
Extensive marketplace for language support and tools
Cross-platform support with remote development capabilities
bestFor: Developers who want a flexible, extensible, and high-performance environment for the full code-build-debug cycle.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a heavy-duty, fully integrated enterprise IDE with complex out-of-the-box workflows and massive project configuration management.
recentUpdates: Version 1.147 (November 2026) introduced experimental support for scheduling agent requests, browser integration for agents, and model routers to optimize task-specific AI usage.
verdict: Visual Studio Code remains the industry-leading editor, now evolving into a sophisticated AI-native platform that bridges local development with autonomous cloud-based agents.

name: Xcode
pricingDetail: The software is free to download. Optional Xcode Cloud compute hours are included with an Apple Developer Program membership (25 hours/month), with additional paid tiers ranging from US$49.99/month for 100 hours to US$3,999/month for 10,000 hours.
description: Xcode is the integrated development environment from Apple used for building, testing, and distributing applications across all Apple platforms including iOS, macOS, and visionOS. It now features an advanced coding assistant capable of leveraging various frontier AI models and autonomous agents to manage project tasks and generate code.
keyFeatures: Agentic coding support for Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and GitHub Copilot
Device Hub for managing physical devices and simulators in one workspace
Instruments for deep system profiling and app performance analysis
Xcode Cloud for continuous integration and delivery
Swift Testing framework and XCTest for robust test automation
bestFor: Developers building native applications for Apple platforms including iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS.
notIdealFor: Developers working primarily on non-Apple platforms, as the software is exclusive to macOS and Apple-silicon hardware.
recentUpdates: Xcode 27.3 beta 2 released on November 16, 2026, introduced GitHub Copilot integration and new localization skills. Xcode 27.2, released in late October 2026, added JSON-based project files (.xcproj) and enhanced Device Hub functionality.
verdict: Xcode is the essential, industry-standard IDE for the Apple ecosystem, now significantly modernized with robust agentic AI capabilities that automate complex development tasks.

name: JetBrains IDEs
pricingDetail: Includes an AI Free tier with limited cloud credits and unlimited code completion/local models, plus paid AI Pro ($20/month) and AI Ultimate ($60/month) tiers offering higher monthly quotas of AI credits. Enterprise options are available for organizations.
description: JetBrains IDEs provide a comprehensive development environment that integrates AI-powered coding assistance and agentic workflows directly into the editor. Through the new JetBrains Air workspace, developers can run third-party coding agents or native features to manage, review, and refactor code within a context-aware IDE.
keyFeatures: JetBrains Air workspace for managing parallel AI agent sessions
In-editor AI code completion and next edit suggestions via Mellum model
Support for third-party coding agents (e.g., Claude Agent, Junie, Codex) via ACP
IDE-native code inspection, debugging, and refactoring for agent-generated code
Presets for saving and reusing agent configurations and instructions
bestFor: Developers working in Java, Kotlin, Python, .NET, C++, or Go who require deep, language-aware IDE tooling combined with the flexibility to choose their own AI coding agents.
notIdealFor: Developers who primarily use light code editors, require highly predictable monthly AI costs for heavy agent usage, or need a stable, unchanging development environment.
recentUpdates: In November 2026, JetBrains released Air in the 2026.3 IDE updates, a new workspace for running and reviewing AI coding agents. Air supports parallel sessions, Git worktrees, and integrates with the IDE's existing refactoring, debugging, and testing tools.
verdict: A comprehensive, high-utility development platform that successfully bridges the gap between modern AI agent autonomy and traditional, professional-grade IDE code intelligence.

name: Visual Studio
pricingDetail: Visual Studio Community is free for individual developers, open-source contributors, academic research, and classroom learning, as well as small non-enterprise organizations. Visual Studio Professional and Enterprise are available via paid subscriptions, with Professional starting at $99.99/mo and Enterprise reaching higher tiers depending on licensing. GitHub Copilot features within the IDE have a free tier (with usage limits) and various paid tiers for individuals (starting at $10/mo) and organizations.
description: Visual Studio is a powerful, Windows-only integrated development environment optimized for .NET, C++, and Windows desktop or game development. It integrates comprehensive coding, debugging, and testing tools with advanced AI-powered assistance via GitHub Copilot.
keyFeatures: AI-powered coding with GitHub Copilot chat, agents, and conflict resolution
Comprehensive debugging, profiling, and diagnostics tools
Built-in support for Azure, SQL, and cross-platform mobile/web development
Bring Your Own Key AI support for models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and others
Solution Explorer with File System and Solution views
bestFor: .NET, C++, and Windows desktop or game developers who require a deep, all-in-one development environment on Windows.
notIdealFor: Developers working on macOS or Linux, polyglot teams needing a consistent cross-platform editor, and large organizations looking for a free IDE solution.
recentUpdates: The November 2026 update (v18.12.1) introduced a new default Copilot Chat experience built on the Copilot SDK, agent-based Git conflict resolution, and improved crash dump debugging with Copilot analysis.
verdict: Visual Studio remains the premier enterprise-grade IDE for the Microsoft ecosystem, now significantly augmented by deeply integrated AI agent workflows that streamline the entire development lifecycle.

name: Copperhead
pricingDetail: The CLI is free and open-source (Apache-2.0). Paid plans include Cloud ($49/user/month), Team ($49/user/month + $199/month platform fee), and custom Enterprise annual licenses.
description: Copperhead is an open-source AI agent designed to automate PCB development within KiCad by managing the design, documentation, and verification loop. It operates as a cursor for circuit boards, ensuring that schematics, bills of materials, and design specifications remain synchronized and verified through automated ERC and DRC checks.
keyFeatures: Automated PCB design verification using native KiCad tools
Full pipeline support from product brief to manufacturing files
Drift detection between design documentation and hardware schematics
Gated workflow requiring validated change proposals before file edits
Deterministic, LLM-free verification checks for use in CI pipelines
bestFor: Hardware engineers and teams looking to automate PCB design, documentation, and synchronization within existing KiCad workflows.
notIdealFor: Users of proprietary EDA software or those seeking a fully automated autorouter, as the tool is specific to KiCad and functions as an agent-driven assistant rather than a black-box layout generator.
recentUpdates: On 2026-11-12, the company announced that Copperhead is now available to everyone for free, disabling billing and including free credits for users. Recent software updates (v0.13.0) include improved firmware stage handling, refined part selection logic, and expanded CLI explain capabilities.
verdict: A powerful, developer-centric tool for hardware teams that treats PCB design like code, enforcing strict synchronization and verification to prevent costly design drift.

name: NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR)
pricingDetail: Free and open-source.
description: NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR) is a local inference tool that creates a cluster from multiple computers on a network to distribute AI inference workloads. It acts as a proxy, routing independent requests to available nodes to maximize compute capacity for concurrent tasks without modifying existing AI applications.
keyFeatures: Workload-aware routing for independent inference requests
Support for Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and vLLM engines
Mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption for secure inter-node communication
Compatibility with OpenAI and Anthropic Messages API formats
Unified management via desktop and terminal interfaces
bestFor: Multi-agent AI workflows and concurrent inference tasks that benefit from distributing parallel requests across multiple local machines.
notIdealFor: Large models requiring pooled GPU memory, requests that must span multiple GPUs, or single, highly sequential tasks where model availability is limited to one node.
recentUpdates: Version 1.0.0 (released October 2026) added native llama.cpp support, RTX Spark hardware validation, and an improved terminal interface with a dedicated Jobs tab.
verdict: An excellent tool for power users looking to maximize idle local compute for parallel AI tasks, provided they have multiple compatible machines on a trusted network.

name: WebLLM
pricingDetail: WebLLM is an open-source project licensed under Apache-2.0, available as a free npm package and for direct use via CDN.
description: WebLLM is a high-performance in-browser inference engine that enables running large language models directly on client devices using WebGPU. It provides an OpenAI-compatible API to facilitate local, private, and server-free AI applications.
keyFeatures: WebGPU-accelerated in-browser inference
Full OpenAI API compatibility (streaming, JSON mode, seeding)
Support for models including Llama, Phi, Gemma, Mistral, and Qwen
Web Worker and Service Worker support for background execution
Custom model integration via MLC format
bestFor: Privacy-focused web applications, offline-capable tools, and browser extensions that require local execution without infrastructure costs.
notIdealFor: High-traffic applications sensitive to CDN egress costs, environments with WebGL-heavy UI elements prone to GPU stalls, or scenarios requiring large frontier models (14B+ parameters) that exceed typical browser VRAM.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.89 (2026-11-17) added MiniCPM5, SmolLM3, and LFM2.5 model support and exposed tokenization via engine APIs. Version 0.2.88 (2026-11-10) addressed prompt echo and logprob fixes. Version 0.2.87 (2026-10-30) updated model binaries and runtime configurations.
verdict: A robust, high-performance solution for running LLMs locally in the browser, ideal for privacy-focused and zero-server architecture projects.

name: Magnitude
pricingDetail: Magnitude is free, open-source software distributed under the Apache 2.0 license with no token costs, paid editions, or managed service tiers.
description: Magnitude is an open-source inference engine that automatically tunes kernels for your specific local hardware to accelerate model performance. It operates as a desktop application and CLI tool designed specifically to provide high-speed, local inference for coding agents.
keyFeatures: On-device kernel tuning for hardware optimization
Built-in speculative decoding with optimized drafters
Quantized KV cache for reduced memory usage
One-click integration with popular coding agents
Cross-platform support for Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, and CPUs
bestFor: Developers running local coding agents on Apple Silicon or NVIDIA hardware who need high-performance, low-latency inference.
notIdealFor: Users needing models outside the curated family catalog, those with older hardware, or engineers requiring enterprise-grade headless deployments.
recentUpdates: As of November 2026, the engine is undergoing a v4 architectural rewrite with 0.3.0 alpha releases in development, following the release of engine v3 and a major catalog update in October 2026.
verdict: Magnitude is an architecturally sophisticated inference engine that justifies its performance claims through real-time kernel compilation, though it currently suits a specific set of supported hardware and model families rather than general-purpose GGUF execution.

name: text-to-cad
pricingDetail: This is a free, open-source tool with no paid tiers, subscriptions, or per-generation costs.
description: text-to-cad is an open-source library of agent skills that enables AI coding assistants to generate and inspect CAD models locally. It uses Python scripts and the build123d library to create manufacturing-ready files like STEP, DXF, and G-code directly on your machine.
keyFeatures: Generation of STEP, GLB, STL, and 3MF files via Python scripting
Manufacturing checks for CNC, sheet metal, and 3D printing
Stress analysis and simulation using CalculiX
Generation of engineering drawings and photorealistic renders
Creation of robot and simulation descriptions like URDF, SRDF, and MJCF
bestFor: Developers and robotics engineers using agents like Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex who need to generate manufacturable parts, robot descriptions, or DXF cut layouts.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a standalone GUI-based CAD application with feature timelines, constraint solvers, or professional multi-user collaboration and support SLAs.
recentUpdates: Version 0.11.17 (2026-11-23) introduced fixes for sheet checks and improved plugin integration. Version 0.11.16 (2026-11-22) added community app support, refined skills, and tool-specific fixes for CNC and lid components.
verdict: An efficient productivity multiplier for developers and makers comfortable with command-line tools who need a direct bridge between text prompts and physical manufacturing files without the overhead of cloud-based CAD.

name: nanochat
pricingDetail: nanochat is free and open-source under the MIT license. The only cost is GPU compute: the reference GPT-2-grade speedrun takes about 2 hours on an 8xH100 node (roughly $48 at ~$3 per GPU-hour, or closer to $15 on spot instances), while small experiments can run on a single GPU, CPU or Apple Silicon.
description: nanochat is a minimal, hackable, and educational codebase designed for training large language models from scratch. It covers the entire pipeline, including tokenization, pretraining, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and inference, all controllable via a single complexity dial.
keyFeatures: End-to-end training pipeline from tokenizer to chat CLI
Single --depth parameter for automated hyperparameter tuning
Public leaderboard for time-to-GPT-2 speedrun benchmarks
Minimalist codebase without complex configuration objects
Support for distributed training on 8xH100 nodes
bestFor: Developers, students, and researchers aiming to learn or experiment with the end-to-end mechanics of LLM training.
notIdealFor: Building production-grade AI assistants or commercial applications, as the models are experimental, prone to hallucinations, and intended for research.
recentUpdates: Development throughout early 2026 focused on pretraining optimizations, achieving GPT-2-grade training in approximately 1.65 hours by March 2026. Recent July 2026 commits added inference benchmarking and execution hardening.
verdict: The clearest hands-on reference for how a modern chat LLM is built end to end, best used as a learning and research harness rather than a model to deploy.

name: colibri
pricingDetail: colibri is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license with no paid tiers; the project accepts optional donations. You only need your own hardware (8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB or more recommended, plus disk space for model weights).
description: colibri is a pure-C inference engine that runs very large mixture-of-experts open models on ordinary computers by keeping the always-active weights in RAM and streaming experts from disk as the model needs them. A one-step setup recommends a model for your machine, builds or downloads the engine and serves OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints that coding agents can use.
keyFeatures: Expert streaming from disk so hundreds-of-billions-parameter MoE models run in modest RAM
CPU, Vulkan and CUDA backends with an optional GPU
Runs published GGUF files as-is, from IQ1_S to Q8_0, F16, BF16 and MXFP4
OpenAI-compatible /v1 and Anthropic-compatible endpoints for coding agents
One-step start-here setup with hardware profiling, model recommendation, resumable downloads and a coli ui dashboard
bestFor: Developers who want to run frontier-scale open MoE models such as GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi or Qwen locally for private coding-agent work without buying datacenter GPUs.
notIdealFor: Latency-sensitive production serving or dense models, since streaming experts from disk trades speed for memory and throughput depends heavily on disk and RAM bandwidth.
recentUpdates: v2.1.0 (October 31, 2026) added native GGUF support on every engine, Mistral-Large-4, Muse Spark Open, Flint and LFM3-VL, CUDA device chains, speculative decoding via MTP heads, 262k-token contexts for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and a new chat UI; v2.0.0 shipped October 6, 2026.
verdict: An impressively compact way to run giant open MoE models on consumer hardware, with agent-ready APIs that make it a practical local backend for coding agents if you can accept disk-bound speeds.

name: FreeToken
pricingDetail: FreeToken is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license, including the Windows and Linux desktop app. There are no paid tiers; you supply your own NVIDIA RTX 30, 40 or 50 series GPU and host memory.
description: FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts inference engine designed to run large frontier-scale open-weight models on personal hardware by treating GPUs, CPUs, and host memory as a unified, elastic platform. It optimizes performance for models that exceed VRAM capacity by adaptively caching active experts and splitting workloads between GPU and system resources.
keyFeatures: Bandwidth-adaptive CPU-GPU co-execution with MoE expert caching
OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible API endpoints
Semantic-aware caching for context reuse in agentic workloads
Support for quantization formats including MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8, and GGUF
Dynamic VRAM re-allocation between expert and KV caches
bestFor: Developers with NVIDIA gaming or workstation GPUs needing to run large 100B-300B+ MoE models locally for agentic coding and tool-calling tasks.
notIdealFor: Users of Apple Silicon, AMD (currently experimental), or CPU-only hardware, as well as those requiring a mature, long-stable, or multi-user enterprise server environment.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.3 (November 23, 2026) introduced speculative decoding support for Gemma-4, added fp8 and int8 per-token head KV cache quantization, and enabled DeepSeek-V4.1 GGUF support.
verdict: A research-backed, fast-moving local MoE server that brings datacenter-style serving techniques to consumer NVIDIA GPUs and is a strong local backend for agent workloads.

name: llama-modchip
pricingDetail: llama-modchip is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license with no paid tiers. You supply your own hardware: 16 to 32 GB of RAM for 30B MoE models or 64 GB for the 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash build.
description: llama-modchip is a high-performance inference engine for running large mixture-of-experts models on CPU-based systems without requiring a dedicated GPU. It utilizes specialized quantization techniques like Fractal-64 and runtime patches to enable the execution of models as large as 284B parameters on standard hardware.
keyFeatures: Fractal-64 and Fractal-MXFP4 quantization
RouteCrack 2.0 speculative engine for high-speed CPU decoding
Native C++ HARP-Cache v2 for millisecond-speed context restoration
Support for CPU-based Split-KV decoding
Unified CLI for setup, benchmarking, and local AI agent integration
bestFor: Developers with 64 GB workstations or high-RAM laptops who need a local backend for running large open-weights models and AI coding agents like Claude Code.
notIdealFor: Users requiring stock compatibility with standard llama.cpp, Ollama, or LM Studio, as the engine uses specialized patched binaries and custom GGUF tensor types.
recentUpdates: Version 3.2.0 released in November 2026 introduced an upstream llama.cpp rebase, quantized heterogeneous Split-KV decode, and native C++ Chained-Prefix HARP-Cache v2 support.
verdict: An ambitious CPU-first MoE runtime that makes very large open models usable on ordinary desktops for local agent work, best treated as an experimental fork until its patches settle.

name: Flide
pricingDetail: Flide is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license and installs from PyPI. You run it on your own NVIDIA GPU; prebuilt kernels cover A10, A40, RTX 30, RTX 50, RTX PRO 6000, H100 and H200.
description: Flide is an extremely fast inference engine designed for Jev-style decision models. It utilizes exact state forking to process multiple questions against a shared state in a single pass, delivering performance up to 9.5 times faster than standard serving engines while maintaining individual-question accuracy.
keyFeatures: Exact state forking via ForkAttention
High-throughput inference for decision models
Support for `/v1/systemone` API compatible with vLLM/SGLang clients
Session caching for multi-step agent trajectories
Gated DeltaNet layers for state consistency
bestFor: Running high-volume decision-making tasks such as email triage or classification where multiple questions must be answered for a single state efficiently.
notIdealFor: Environments without NVIDIA GPU hardware, non-Linux operating systems (excluding WSL2), or tasks requiring general-purpose LLM completion engines where standard sampling behavior is preferred over exact state forking.
recentUpdates: Recent releases include support for Gemma 4 agent sessions (v0.1.20), the addition of models like Copernicus-31B and liquamen (v0.1.19), and native Docker image support (v0.1.19) as of late November 2026.
verdict: A fast-moving, specialised serving engine for the Jev decision model ecosystem; its speed claims are vendor benchmarks and it is still pre-1.0.

name: Caw
pricingDetail: Free and open source under the MIT licence. You download a single binary for Linux, macOS (Apple Silicon) or Windows and run it locally; the agents it launches use your own subscriptions or API keys.
description: Caw is a web terminal multiplexer for AI coding agents. It runs a local server, detects the CLI agents installed on your machine and opens each one in a browser terminal pane, with a live status board, per-agent git worktrees, push notifications and usage-limit tracking.
keyFeatures: Runs Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Antigravity, Pi, Hermes and other CLI agents side by side in the browser
Agent Control Center Kanban board showing Working, Needs Input or Idle from each agent transcript
Automatic isolated git worktree and branch per agent
Push notifications on desktop or phone when an agent needs input or finishes
Live usage limits and reset times for Claude, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode, Ollama, OpenRouter, Zed and more
bestFor: Developers who run several CLI coding agents at once and want to watch and answer them from one browser tab, including from a phone.
notIdealFor: Teams that need a hosted, multi-user agent platform, or developers who prefer a native terminal app over a browser interface.
recentUpdates: v0.3.7 shipped on November 1, 2026, following v0.3.6 on September 6, 2026; the project launched on Product Hunt as an open-source web interface for AI agents.
verdict: A lightweight, self-hosted way to supervise many CLI agents from a browser; still pre-1.0 and maintained by a small team.

name: GitHits
pricingDetail: The CLI and MCP server are open source under Apache-2.0. The hosted index launched as a free beta in June 2026 and needs a GitHits account; the company said a commercial version would follow, and no pricing page was published as of November 26, 2026.
description: GitHits gives AI coding agents a version-aware index of open-source code, documentation and package data. Through an MCP server, CLI or REST API, agents can search and read dependency source at the exact version they use, find source-cited examples, and check package health before changing code.
keyFeatures: Search, grep and read dependency source and docs at a specific package version or repository ref
Source-cited code examples from real open-source projects
Package inspection for dependencies, licences, vulnerabilities and changelogs, plus upgrade reviews and version diffs
`npx githits@latest init` configures Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Cline, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Zed and more
Public REST API and githits-scan for SBOMs and lockfile audits
bestFor: Developers whose coding agents guess at third-party library behaviour and need source-backed answers about the dependencies they use or plan to upgrade.
notIdealFor: Work that depends mainly on private or proprietary libraries, or teams that cannot send queries to a hosted service.
recentUpdates: CLI and MCP v0.41.0 (November 19, 2026) added package lifecycle evidence and unified vulnerability findings; githits-scan 0.6.0 and 0.6.1 (November 19 and 20, 2026) added audit presentation JSON and upgrade dependency checks.
verdict: A focused context layer for the code beyond your repository, shipping weekly; the hosted index is still labelled beta and pricing is not yet published.

name: VT Code
pricingDetail: Free and open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0. You bring your own model access: an API key for a hosted provider, a ChatGPT subscription login for OpenAI, a GitHub Copilot login, or a local model through Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp.
description: VT Code is an open-source coding agent written in Rust. One shared runloop powers a terminal TUI and a native macOS app, with read-only planning, turn diffs, a sandboxed command policy and resumable headless runs, and it can use many hosted or local model providers per task.
keyFeatures: Terminal TUI and native macOS desktop app sharing the same agent runloop, sessions and config
Read-only planning mode, turn diff review and a sandboxed, auditable command policy
Resumable headless exec mode with snapshots and subagents
MCP, skills, plugins, ACP for editors such as Zed, and a WebMCP editor
Per-task providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp
bestFor: Developers who want an open-source, provider-agnostic terminal coding agent with strict execution policy and the option of a native Mac app.
notIdealFor: Teams that want a hosted, managed agent service, or Windows and Intel Mac users who want a packaged desktop app (the desktop cask ships Apple Silicon builds only).
recentUpdates: v0.185.3 shipped on November 27, 2026 with streaming, MCP preview and accessibility fixes, following v0.185.2 on November 24, 2026, which patched RUSTSEC advisories and tightened sandbox and shell preflight checks.
verdict: A fast-moving, security-minded open-source alternative to closed terminal agents, maintained mainly by one developer with near-daily releases.

name: MulmoTerminal
pricingDetail: Free and open source under the MIT licence. You run it locally with `npx mulmoterminal@latest`; the agents it launches use your own subscriptions or API keys.
description: MulmoTerminal is a browser terminal for running several AI coding agents in parallel. Each session runs in its own real pty cell, colour-coded by state, with a roster of every session, git worktree isolation, cost readouts and phone notifications when an agent finishes or needs input.
keyFeatures: Grid of live agent sessions colour-coded working, done or needs you, with an attention chime
Claude Code by default plus Codex, Antigravity, Grok, Muse, GitHub Copilot CLI and Cursor CLI
tmux-backed sessions that survive server restarts
One-click git worktrees with diff, commit, push and open PR from each cell
Web Push and a RemoteHost companion to answer agents from a phone
bestFor: Developers who run many CLI coding agents at once and lose track of which session is waiting for them.
notIdealFor: Developers who run a single agent at a time, or teams that need a hosted, multi-user agent platform.
recentUpdates: v13.10.0 shipped on November 27, 2026 with two new built-in themes, following v13.9.0 on November 26, 2026, which stopped background git reads from colliding with your own git commands.
verdict: A polished, actively maintained local cockpit for supervising parallel coding agents, shipping several releases a week.
